deviationRules.reason: Constructors are shown by their surface keyword.

sections.title: Syntax
sections.intro: Programs are terms of a call-by-value $\lambda$-calculus with session-typed channels. Terms never mention points. Points appear in types and in the relation, where they order the waits of threads.

blocks.title: Terms
blocks.caption: Thirteen term formers with de Bruijn variables. A box $!e$ binds itself in $e$, and $k$ ranges over the constants.
blocks.why: Typing has one rule per term former, and the semantics one head step per redex.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Derived let
blocks.formula: \sym{syn.let}{\mathsf{let}\ a = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2 \ \triangleq\ \mathsf{let}\ \langle a, u\rangle = \langle e_1, \ast\rangle\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{let}\ \ast = u\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2}
blocks.caption: The one-variable $\mathsf{let}$ is notation for a pair followed by a unit elimination, with $u$ fresh.
blocks.why: Examples read better with a one-variable $\mathsf{let}$. As notation it needs no typing rule of its own.

deviations.reason: Derived form, defined in Syntax.v as an application of a $\lambda$.

blocks.title: Constants
blocks.caption: The channel operations are constants. $\mathsf{send}$ takes a pair $\langle v, o\rangle$, $\mathsf{link}$ a pair of ends and $\mathsf{spawn}$ a thunk.
blocks.why: As constants applied to values, the channel operations need no syntax of their own, and each has an ordinary function type.

blocks.title: Values
blocks.formula: \sym{syn.values}{v ::= \ast \mid o \mid k \mid \lambda e \mid\ !e \mid \langle v_1, v_2\rangle \mid \mathsf{inj}_i\,v}
blocks.caption: Unit, ends, constants, abstractions and boxes are values, and so are pairs and injections of values.
blocks.why: A thread that is a value has finished. The value relation $V$ is defined on values.

blocks.title: Ends
blocks.formula: \sym{end.cend}{o ::= c^{+} \mid c^{-}} \qquad \sym{end.dual}{\overline{c^{+}} = c^{-}\quad \overline{c^{-}} = c^{+}} \qquad \sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}(c^{\pm}) = c}
blocks.caption: An end $o$ belongs to the channel $\mathsf{ech}\,o$, and $\overline{o}$ is the other end of that channel.
blocks.why: Two threads hold the two ends of a channel. Naming ends instead of channels gives each end its own type, point and counter.

blocks.title: Ends a term mentions
blocks.formula: \sym{syn.fends}{\mathsf{fends}(e)} \qquad \sym{syn.fchans}{\mathsf{fchans}(e) = \mathsf{ech}[\mathsf{fends}(e)]}
blocks.caption: $\mathsf{fends}(e)$ is the set of ends in $e$, and $\mathsf{fchans}(e)$ the set of their channels.
blocks.why: The relation reads ownership off terms. A closure or a payload owns exactly the ends in it, and the relation checks this when a value is spawned or sent.

blocks.title: Processes and configurations
blocks.caption: A process is a finite set $C$ of restricted channels and a finite multiset $E$ of threads. A configuration names its threads by $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.
blocks.why: A running program is a set of threads together with its private channels. A channel is restricted when both of its ends are inside the process.

blocks.title: Points
blocks.caption: A point $x$ has a root, a constant $a$ or a variable $\iota$. $\overline{x}$ flips its polarity, $x^{+}$ raises its offset, and $x\cdot\kappa$ is one of its fields.
blocks.why: Points order the waits of threads. Each end has a point, and a thread may wait at a point only below the points of the ends it still holds.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Where an end moves
blocks.caption: An action moves an end from $x$ to $x^{+}$, and a choice moves it to a field of $x$. The $j$-th payload end of a message at $x$ arrives at $x\cdot j$.
blocks.why: The point of an end changes as its protocol advances. One point per end therefore describes a whole protocol, and no action needs a point of its own.
blocks.example: An end at $x$ that sends twice is at $x^{++}$ afterwards.

blocks.title: Field labels
blocks.formula: \sym{lbl.field}{\kappa \in \mathbb{N}}
blocks.caption: Field labels $\kappa$ are natural numbers, and $x\cdot\kappa$ is the field $\kappa$ of the point $x$.
blocks.why: Fields give payload ends and the continuations of a choice points of their own, each related to the point of the carrier.

blocks.title: Link substitution
blocks.formula: \sym{link.csub}{\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2\,(o) = \begin{cases} o_2 & o = \overline{o_1} \\ \overline{o_2} & o = o_1 \\ o & o \notin \{o_1, \overline{o_1}\} \end{cases}}
blocks.caption: A link of $o_1$ and $o_2$ renames $\overline{o_1}$ to $o_2$ in the other threads, so that the two remaining ends form one channel.
blocks.why: After a link, the threads holding $\overline{o_1}$ and $\overline{o_2}$ communicate with each other directly.

sections.title: Semantics
sections.intro: A thread steps with a label, and a process steps by one or two thread steps. The section ends with the three properties the theorems establish, deadlock freedom, absence of internal divergence and lock freedom.

blocks.title: Thread labels
blocks.caption: The label $\beta$ stands for application, unit and pair elimination, case and force. A session label $\sigma$ is an action offered on an end.
blocks.why: An internal step needs no other thread. A session label must be matched by the dual label of another thread.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Head steps (T-Act rules)
blocks.caption: One head step per redex. $\mathsf{recv}\,o$ has a step for each value $v$ it may receive.
blocks.why: Because a receive steps for each possible value, the step of a thread is defined without the other thread of the channel.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Evaluation frames (T-Act-Ctx)
blocks.formula: \dfrac{\sym{T-Act-Ctx}{e \xrightarrow{\alpha} e'}\quad \sym{sem.frameval}{\mathsf{frame\_val}\,f}}{\sym{se.frame}{f[e]} \xrightarrow{\alpha} f[e']}\;\textsf{T-Act-Ctx}
blocks.caption: Steps lift through one evaluation frame $f$ at a time, never under $\lambda$ or $!$.
blocks.why: Evaluation is call by value from left to right. A $\lambda$ or a box delays its body until it is applied or forced.

blocks.title: Process steps (P-Act rules)
blocks.formula:
\begin{array}{l}
\sym{P-Act-Beta}{M(i) \xrightarrow{\beta} e'} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C, \sym{se.upd}{M[i \mapsto e']}) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-New}{M(i) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} e',\ \sym{sem.fresh-global}{c \notin C \cup \sym{se.echans}{\mathsf{echans}(M)}}} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C \cup \{c\}, M[i\mapsto e']) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Spawn}{M(i) \xrightarrow{\mathsf{spawn}\,v} e',\ j \notin \mathsf{dom}\,M} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C, M[i\mapsto e'][j \mapsto v\,\ast]) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Msg}{M(i) \xrightarrow{o!v} e',\ M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o}?v} f',\ i \neq j} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C, M[i\mapsto e'][j\mapsto f']) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Close}{M(i) \xrightarrow{o\,\mathsf{end}} e',\ M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o}\,\mathsf{end}} f',\ i \neq j,\ \sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o \in C} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C \setminus \{\sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o\}, M[i\mapsto e'][j\mapsto f']) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Choice}{M(i) \xrightarrow{o\lhd b} e',\ M(j) \xrightarrow{\overline{o}\rhd b} f',\ i \neq j} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C, M[i\mapsto e'][j\mapsto f']) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Link}{M(i) \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1,o_2\}} e',\ \sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o_1 \in C} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C\setminus\{\sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o_1\}, \sym{link.csub}{\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2} \circ M[i\mapsto e']) \\[4pt]
\sym{P-Act-Session}{M(i) \xrightarrow{\sigma} e',\ \sym{se.subj}{\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma} \cap C = \varnothing} \\ \qquad \Rightarrow\ (C \setminus \sym{sem.sentc}{\mathsf{sentc}\,\sigma}, M[i\mapsto e'])
\end{array}
blocks.caption: Each rule combines the steps of one or two threads into a step of the configuration $(C, M)$.
blocks.why: A message pairs a send and a receive on the two ends of one channel. Internal steps involve one thread.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Events
blocks.caption: An event records the threads $\mathsf{parts}(ev)$ that took part in a step, and the channel or ends of the step.
blocks.why: Lock freedom is stated in terms of the threads that take part in steps, which the event of each step records.

blocks.title: Properties
blocks.caption: A process is deadlock free when each reachable process has terminated or can step. \inmode{lf}{It has no internal divergence when no reachable process runs internal steps forever. It is lock free when, on each weakly fair maximal run, a waiting thread later takes part in a step.}
blocks.why: The theorems establish these properties for typed processes.

sections.title: Types and worlds
sections.intro: Types give each end a session type and a point. Worlds order the points, and typing and the relation read the order of one world. \inmode{lf}{Lock-free types add credits to ends and closures, and costs and ticket needs to arrows and judgments.}

blocks.title: Types

variants.df: \begin{array}{rl} T, U ::= & \sym{ty.unit}{\ast} \mid \sym{ty.arrow}{T \multimap^{\sym{ty.arrow.ub}{u}}_{\sym{ty.arrow.lb}{l}} U} \mid \sym{ty.prod}{T \otimes U} \mid \sym{ty.sum}{T \oplus U} \mid \sym{ty.sess}{S@x} \\ \mid & \sym{ty.box}{\Box(\forall \sym{pt.var}{\bar\iota}\, \sym{ty.box.svars}{\bar\alpha}.\ \sym{ty.box.constraint}{C}.\ \ast \multimap^{u} U)} \mid \sym{ty.ex}{\exists^{\sym{ty.ex.lb}{l}} \bar\iota.\ C.\ T} \end{array}

blocks.caption: $S@x$ is an end with session type $S$ at the point $x$. An arrow has an upper point $u$ and a lower bound $l$, and a box quantifies over points and session types under a constraint $C$. \inmode{lf}{Credits $a$ appear on ends and on closures, the two kinds of value that hold ends themselves. \inmode{lf}{The credit of an end is a lower bound on its counter.} \inmode{lf}{The credit of a closure is a lower bound on its captured counters above the floor $h$.}}
blocks.why: A type says what a value is and, for an end, at which point it waits. \inmode{lf}{A credit bounds how long the thread holding an end may postpone it.}

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: Session types
blocks.caption: Session types with sequencing $S.S$ and recursion, read through $\mathsf{unfold}(S)$. A payload binds point variables $\bar\iota$, which stand for the fields of the carrier.
blocks.why: A session type describes the protocol of one end. The typing rules read its first action after unfolding recursion and leading $\mathsf{Skip}$.

blocks.title: Duality
blocks.caption: $\mathsf{dual}$ swaps sending and receiving and keeps payloads, $\mathsf{Skip}$ and $\mathsf{Close}$. We write $\overline{S}$ for $\mathsf{dual}\,S$.
blocks.why: The two ends of a channel follow dual protocols. Creation, linking and composition check duality.

blocks.title: Session equivalence
blocks.caption: $S \simeq S'$ when the two session types describe the same protocol. $\approx$ is $\simeq$ after erasing annotations, and $\mathsf{sdual}$ is duality up to annotations.
blocks.why: With recursion and $\mathsf{Skip}$ one protocol has many spellings, and the rules compare session types up to $\simeq$.

blocks.title: Active points and lower bounds
blocks.caption: $\mathsf{ap}(T)$ is the set of dual points of the ends in a value of $T$. A thread holding such a value may wait only below these points. Hidden ends contribute $\bot$, which no fact orders against a point, so a check against a value with hidden ends fails.
blocks.why: A thread that waits while it holds a value must wait below the dual points of the ends in that value, and $\mathsf{ap}$ computes these points from the type.

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: Payloads
blocks.caption: A payload $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ mentions only its own point variables $\iota_0, \ldots, \iota_{m-1}$. A message at the carrier point $x$ places them at the fields $x\cdot 0, \ldots, x\cdot(m{-}1)$.
blocks.why: A payload is described relative to the end that sends it, so one session type serves each point the end may have.

blocks.title: Annotations and ticket needs
blocks.caption: Credits $a$, costs $c$, floors $h$ and the counter bound $N$ are numbers or $\infty$. A term that must keep $r$ link tickets needs $\vartheta(r)$ tickets when it starts, and $tk$ tickets suffice when $\vartheta(r) \leq tk$. A link adds one to the need, a spawn doubles the rest, and sequencing composes needs. With every annotation at $\infty$, written $\mathsf{ty\_df}$, lock-free typing is deadlock-free typing.
blocks.why: These are the numbers lock-free typing adds to types and judgments. At $\infty$ each premise about them holds.

blocks.title: Kinds of types
blocks.caption: $\mathsf{tfree}\,T$ holds for the types whose values hold no end, and P-Term asks it of the result type of a process. $\mathsf{unlimited}\,T$ holds for the types that may be copied and dropped.
blocks.why: Process results hold no end, only unlimited types may be copied or dropped, and values without ends do not age.

blocks.title: Worlds
blocks.formula: \sym{w.world}{W = (\sym{w.consts}{A}, \sym{w.facts}{\prec_A})}
blocks.caption: A world $W$ has a set of roots $A$ and facts $\prec_A$ between points with roots in $A$.
blocks.why: Typing and the relation read the order of one world. Each creation adds roots and facts.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: The order of a world
blocks.caption: $\prec_W$ is the transitive closure $\mathsf{tc}$ of the facts together with $x \prec x^{+}$ and $x \prec \overline{x}^{+}$.
blocks.why: Besides the stated facts, the order says that an end moves up as its protocol advances.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

blocks.title: Well-formed, strict and well-founded worlds
blocks.caption: Each result asks for a strict world. \inmode{lf}{Lock freedom also asks for a well-founded one.}
blocks.why: In a cyclic order two threads waiting on each other would both count as ready, so the results ask for strict worlds. \inmode{lf}{Lock-free adequacy proceeds by induction along the order, which needs well-foundedness.}

blocks.title: Extension, growth, join, restriction
blocks.caption: Extension $\sqsubseteq$, growth $W \oplus C$ by the facts of a creation, and the join $\sqcup$. A join is strict when both worlds are and their restrictions to the shared roots $S = A_1 \cap A_2$ join strictly.
blocks.why: Worlds grow during a run, and the relation holds in each larger world. Composition joins two worlds and checks only their shared roots.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field.

sections.title: Typing
sections.intro: The typing judgment assigns each term a type under a context of facts, ends and variables, and a future, the points at which the context acts after the term. Its rules check the order facts a thread needs when it waits. Process typing builds processes from typed threads. \inmode{lf}{Lock-free typing adds credits, costs and ticket needs at a finite counter bound $N$, and the guard.}

blocks.title: Credits

rows.text: a lower bound on the counter of an end, or of the ends a closure captured
rows.label: credit

rows.text: the term performs at most $c$ actions before it returns
rows.label: cost

rows.text: what is held while $e$ runs loses $c$, and each credit must be at least $c$
an idle end loses credit without the check
an action returns its end with credit $N$
a sent end loses one
rows.label: transfer

rows.text: the body of a closure sees each captured end at its credit minus $a$
a spawned closure has credit at least one, so the ends of the child lose one

blocks.caption: Each end has a counter at run time, the number of actions the thread holding it may perform on other ends before it must act on this end. A credit is a lower bound on that counter, so the holding thread postpones an end only finitely often. Aging lowers the credits of held values by the cost of the code that runs, an action restores its own end to $N$, and transferring an end to another thread lowers its credit by one.
blocks.why: Credits rule out a holding thread that acts on other ends forever while a partner waits, and an end that is passed between threads forever.
blocks.example: Postponement and endless delegation in the Examples tab have no lock-free typing.

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: Tickets

rows.text: the tickets a term needs at its start to keep $r$ tickets at its end
rows.label: need

rows.text: $tk$ tickets suffice
a link uses one ticket
a spawn gives the child half the tickets, so the need doubles
sequencing composes needs, and is defined when the result is again a pair
P-Term requires a finite need for each thread

blocks.caption: Each thread has a number of link tickets, a link uses one, and no step creates tickets. A ticket need $\vartheta$ says how many tickets a term needs, and P-Term requires the need of each thread to be finite. A thread therefore performs finitely many links.
blocks.why: A link acts on no end, so counters do not bound links, and a link gives the waiting thread a new dual end with a full counter. Tickets rule out a thread that relinks forever.
blocks.example: Link refresh in the Examples tab has no lock-free typing.

blocks.title: The guard

rows.text: $t$ uses the variable of a box only after a session action
rows.label: guard

rows.text: a box marks its own variable
a marked variable cannot be used
each evaluation of $e$ to a value performs a session action, after which the marks are cleared
each thread of the process is guarded

blocks.caption: Internal steps ($\beta$, $\mathsf{new}$, $\mathsf{spawn}$, $\mathsf{link}$) change no counter. The guard requires each recursive call to come after a session action, so a thread cannot take internal steps forever.
blocks.why: A loop made only of internal steps runs forever without acting with any other thread. Deadlock freedom allows such a loop and lock freedom does not.
blocks.example: Guard rejections in the Examples tab, such as $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$.

blocks.title: A well-founded world

rows.text: the order has no infinite descending chain
rows.label: well-founded

rows.text: a premise of lock-free soundness, which no typing rule checks

blocks.caption: A waiting thread waits on the thread holding its dual end, which may itself wait at a lower point. In a well-founded order this chain of waits ends, and the thread at its bottom can act.
blocks.why: It rules out a chain of waiting threads that grows forever, each waiting below the previous one.
blocks.example: The growing waiting chain in the Examples tab is outside lock-free soundness.

blocks.title: The typing judgment
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{tj.Gamma}{\Gamma} ; \sym{tj.Delta}{\Delta} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\sym{tj.F}{F}}_{\sym{tj.W}{W}\inmode{lf}{,\sym{tj.N}{N}}} e : T\inmode{lf}{\ \sym{tj.eff}{!}\ \varepsilon} \\ \sym{tj.held}{F \triangleleft H = F \cup \sym{ty.heads}{\mathsf{ap}}(H)}\inmode{lf}{\ \land\ \sym{tj.hage}{\mathsf{def}(H - c)}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\ }\inmode{lf}{\sym{tj.eff}{\varepsilon = (c, \vartheta)} \qquad \sym{tj.seq}{\sym{ann.tok}{\mathsf{tok}}\,\vartheta_1\,\vartheta_2 \Rightarrow \varepsilon_1 \cdot \varepsilon_2 = (c_1 + c_2,\ \vartheta_1 \circ \vartheta_2)}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\ }\inmode{lf}{\sym{tj.zero}{0 = (0, \hat 1)} \qquad \sym{tj.one}{1 = (1, \hat 1)} \qquad \sym{tp.max}{\max(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)} \qquad \sym{E-Sub.cost}{\varepsilon \leq \varepsilon'}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: $\Gamma$ holds facts, $\Delta$ the ends and variables, and $F$ is the future. $F \triangleleft H$ adds to the future the active points of what the thread holds while $e$ runs. The world $W$ and the counter bound $N$ stay fixed for a whole derivation, and the rules leave them implicit. In the lock-free mode $\varepsilon$ is the effect of $e$.
blocks.why: Several rules run one subterm while the thread holds the values of others. Writing the future as $F \triangleleft H$ states once what these rules need, the future of the running subterm extended by the active points of the held values.
blocks.example: E-App runs $e_1$ while holding $\Delta_2$, written $\Gamma ; \Delta_1 \vdash^{F \triangleleft \Delta_2} e_1 : \ldots$

blocks.title: Contexts and the fact theory
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{tj.Delta}{\Delta : o \mapsto (S@x)\inmode{lf}{\inmode{lf}{^{a}}},\ i \mapsto T} \qquad \sym{ctx.lsplit}{\Delta = \Delta_1, \Delta_2} \\ \sym{tj.Gamma}{\Gamma = (\sym{ctx.hyps}{(C, \bar x)^{*}}, \sym{ctx.fvar}{\varphi \mapsto u})} \qquad \sym{ctx.slt}{\Gamma \vdash x \prec y} \\ \sym{tj.F}{F = (X, \sym{ctx.fvarF}{\varphi} \mid \sym{ctx.bot}{\bot})}\end{array}
blocks.caption: The rules read order facts only through $\Gamma \vdash x \prec y$. It is the least transitive relation containing $\prec_W$, the facts $C[\bar x]$ of the instances in $\Gamma$, and $u \prec \varphi$ for the future variables $\varphi \mapsto u$ in $\Gamma$.
blocks.why: The rules split $\Delta$ between subterms and extend $\Gamma$ under boxes and existentials. The block defines the two contexts and the order judgment $\Gamma \vdash x \prec y$.

blocks.title: Side conditions on points
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{side.ub}{u \prec F \iff (\forall y \in X.\ \Gamma \mathrel{\sym{ctx.slt}{\vdash}} u \prec y) \land (F = (X, \varphi) \Rightarrow \Gamma \mathrel{\sym{ctx.slt}{\vdash}} u \prec \varphi) \land F \neq (X, \bot)} \\ \sym{side.top}{\top \prec F \iff F = (\varnothing, \cdot)} \qquad \sym{E-Send.heads}{x \prec T \iff \forall y \in \sym{ty.heads}{\mathsf{ap}}(T).\ \Gamma \mathrel{\sym{ctx.slt}{\vdash}} x \prec y} \qquad \sym{side.lb}{l \preccurlyeq \Delta \iff \forall y \in \sym{ty.heads}{\mathsf{ap}}(\Delta).\ \Gamma \mathrel{\sym{ctx.slt}{\vdash}} l \preccurlyeq y} \qquad \sym{side.hold}{\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]}\end{array}
blocks.caption: $u \prec F$ says that $u$ lies below the points of $F$. $x \prec T$ says that $x$ lies below the dual points of the ends in $T$. $l \preccurlyeq \Delta$ says that $l$ lies at or below the dual points of $\Delta$, and $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$ that the facts of $C$ at $\bar x$ are derivable.
blocks.why: These are the order checks of typing. A term never waits above a point at which its context acts later, and a thread waits only below the dual points of the values it holds.
blocks.breaks: Without them the type system is plain GV and the cycle of two threads closing two channels in opposite orders types.

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: Aging
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{c}\dfrac{\begin{array}{c}\sym{age.free}{\sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T}\end{array}}{T - c = T}\;\textsf{Age-Free} \qquad \dfrac{\begin{array}{c}\sym{age.credit}{c \leq a}\end{array}}{(S@x)\inmode{lf}{^{a}} - c = (S@x)^{a - c}}\;\textsf{Age-Credit} \\[2ex] \dfrac{\begin{array}{c}\sym{age.idle}{\sym{fu.idle}{\mathsf{idle}}\,S}\end{array}}{(S@x)\inmode{lf}{^{a}} - c = (S@x)^{\max(a - c, 0)}}\;\textsf{Age-Idle} \qquad \dfrac{\begin{array}{c}\sym{age.credit}{c \leq a}\end{array}}{(T \mathrel{\sym{ty.arrow}{\multimap}} U)\inmode{lf}{^{a}} - c = (T \mathrel{\sym{ty.arrow}{\multimap}} U)^{a - c}}\;\textsf{Age-Arr} \\[2ex] \sym{age.agg}{(T_1 \otimes T_2) - c = (T_1 - c) \otimes (T_2 - c) \qquad (T_1 \oplus T_2) - c = (T_1 - c) \oplus (T_2 - c) \qquad (\exists^{l}\bar\iota.\,C.\,T) - c = \exists^{l}\bar\iota.\,C.\,(T - c)}\end{array}\end{array}
blocks.caption: $T - c$ lowers the credits of the ends and closures in $T$ by $c$. It requires $c \leq a$ for ends that are not idle and for closures, and leaves $\mathsf{tfree}$ types unchanged. A captured end needs credit $h + a$, and the body of the closure sees it at credit $h$.
blocks.why: An action of the thread postpones the ends the thread holds by one step. Aging records this on the types of held values, and capture records it for the ends a closure takes along.

blocks.why: A value may forget facts it does not need. Admissible weakening and contraction keep the rule set free of structural rules.

blocks.caption: P-Term types one thread $t$ that holds both ends of each channel in $C_0$, at dual types and points, over an interface $\Sigma$ without partner pairs. P-Connect cuts two components at $\Sigma_C$ against $\overline{\Sigma_C}$ and compares only the shared roots of the two worlds. \inmode{lf}{Lock-free process typing is process typing at a finite counter bound $N$ with each thread guarded.}
blocks.why: Processes are built from single threads by P-Term and composed by P-Connect.

blocks.title: The guard
blocks.caption: $\mathsf{acts}\,e$ holds when each evaluation of $e$ to a value performs a session action. The guard marks the variable of a box as unusable until the body has acted. A process is guarded when each of its threads is.
blocks.why: A thread that recurses without a session action makes internal steps forever. The guard rejects such recursion.

sections.title: Semantic typing
sections.intro: The logical relation defines when a value, a term and a process are safe, by induction on a step index. Typed programs are safe by the fundamental theorems, and safe closed processes are deadlock free by adequacy. \inmode{lf}{For lock freedom we read the same relation with other step costs, add fuel to each thread, and combine the two in the lock-free process relation.}

blocks.title: Reading the relations
blocks.caption: The relations are indexed by a world $W$, whose order they read, and a level $n$, the number of steps for which they guarantee safety. A term is safe when it is a safe value, or when it is ready and each of its steps leads to a safe term one level lower. Readiness says that a stuck term waits below the dual points of the ends it holds. Processes are safe in the same way and remain safe when their ends are fused, so composing two safe processes needs no further proof. \inmode{lf}{Fuel is a second predicate on each thread, and the lock-free process relation requires both of every thread.}
blocks.why: Each row says in words what one judgment of this section means.

blocks.title: Step costs
blocks.caption: The number of levels each kind of step consumes in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{A cost table $\kappa$ assigns these numbers subject to three conditions. The lock-free relation uses $\kappa_L$, in which internal steps are free.}
blocks.why: The costs fix how far the level drops at a step. \inmode{lf}{A step of cost $0$ is read at the same level, so a thread cannot take infinitely many of them.}

blocks.title: The value relation
blocks.caption: Each rule is one clause of $V$, by recursion on the type within a level, and $\Theta$ maps exactly the ends the value owns. A closure is safe when its body is safe in each larger world, at each lower level, for each argument and each future of the caller above $u$. A thunk, the closure that $\mathsf{spawn}$ runs, is read at the empty future. A box owns no end, and it is safe when $\mathsf{thunk}(e) = \lambda\_.\,e[!e]$ is safe at each instance. An existential value is a value of the body at witness points whose facts hold.
blocks.why: The clauses for closures, thunks and boxes quantify over larger worlds and lower levels. This quantification makes the relation compositional.

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: The term relation
blocks.caption: A term in $E$ is a value in $V$ when it is irreducible and ready when it is reducible, and each of its steps meets its obligation. The successor is read one level lower, or at the same level after a free step.
blocks.why: The term relation is the center of the logical relation. Values, obligations and readiness are its three clauses.

blocks.title: Obligations of term steps
blocks.caption: Each step $e \xrightarrow{\alpha} e'$ of a term holding $\Theta$ must meet $\mathsf{Obl}_\alpha(e')$. A $\beta$ step keeps the ends. A spawn gives the child exactly the ends of its thunk, and a creation adds two dual ends at a fresh root or at a field. A send gives away exactly the ends of its payload, and a receive is safe for each value that may arrive. A close removes the end, a choice moves it to the field of the branch, and a link removes two dual ends.
blocks.why: The obligations say how each step changes ownership and points. The relation reads step labels only here.

blocks.title: Readiness
blocks.caption: Readiness constrains a stuck term, one that can only offer actions. A stuck term has finished when it offers nothing, and each end it offers lies below the dual points of the ends it keeps and below its future. A stuck process is at a link, or has finished when it offers nothing, and each interface end it keeps has an offered end below its dual point. Internal channels have no points.
blocks.why: In a strict order some stuck thread waits at a minimal point, and the thread holding the dual end can act with that thread. Adequacy uses this argument to derive deadlock freedom from readiness.

blocks.caption: Internal steps, including messages between two threads of $p$, keep the interface. A message with the outside moves ends across the interface. A send gives away its payload ends, including the ends $\Theta_e$ of internal channels, and a receive must be safe for each value that may arrive at each lower level.
blocks.why: Each case says how the interface changes at a step and where the successor must be safe.

blocks.title: Relation and fuel side by side
blocks.caption: Fuel is a second predicate on a thread, separate from the relation and with the same shape, a value clause and one obligation per step. The relation gives each end a point, $S@x$, and fuel gives it a counter, $S^f$, and also counts link tickets $tk$. The lock-free process relation requires both of each thread. The relation makes a stuck thread ready, and fuel bounds how often the thread holding a dual end acts on other ends first.
blocks.why: This table compares what the relation and fuel read and guarantee, and shows that the lock-free process relation is where they meet.

blocks.title: Fuel
blocks.caption: Fuel has the shape of the term relation $E$ without the ready clause. $e \in F^N_n\llbracket \Phi ; tk \vdash \sigma\ !\ (d, r)\rrbracket$ says that the thread $e$, which holds the ends $\Phi$ and $tk$ link tickets, has fuel for $n$ more steps. When $e$ is a value it is in $FV$ at $\sigma$ and keeps $r$ tickets. Otherwise each step meets its fuel obligation one level lower. The clauses hold for each larger counter bound $N'$ and each injective renaming $g$ of ends, because a link in another thread renames ends. $\mathsf{fsem}$ is fuel at each level with each counter at $N$, and it is the only fuel statement independent of the level.
blocks.why: Fuel bounds how often a thread acts on other ends before it acts on an end it holds. Lock-free adequacy measures waits with these counters and tickets.

blocks.title: Fuel obligations
blocks.caption: An action on $o$ requires $o$ held and not idle, and a positive counter on the other ends that are not idle and on the frame. It uses one unit of the frame, advances the protocol of $o$, resets the counter of $o$ to $N$ and decrements the other counters, written $\Phi{\downarrow}[o \mapsto S^{N}]$. Internal steps decrement no counter. A new channel starts both ends at $N$. A spawn transfers the ends of the thunk to the child with counters one lower and gives the child half the tickets. A link removes two dual ends and uses one ticket. A send transfers its payload ends with counters one lower, and a receive continues for each value in $FV$ that may arrive.
blocks.why: Each kind of step changes the held ends, counters and tickets in one way, the same at each level.

blocks.title: Values with fuel
blocks.caption: Values with fuel by recursion on the type. The counter of an end is at least its credit. A closure keeps its captured counters at least at the floor $h$ plus its credit, and its body has fuel at each call. A box holds no end, and its body has fuel at each force.
blocks.why: Values with fuel connect credits in types with counters at run time.

deviations.reason: Generalized arrows (upper point ⊤, lower point ⊥) and per-end capture are planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12). The Rocq still has the floor h with capture, E-SpawnLam and V-Thunk.

blocks.title: The lock-free process relation
blocks.formula:
\begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{c}
\sym{sp.state}{a = (q, K, tk)} \qquad \sym{sp.hold}{K : \mathsf{End} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N} \times \mathsf{Point} \times (\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\})} \qquad \sym{sp.tk}{tk : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}} \\
\sym{sp.next}{\mathsf{lf\_next}^{\chi}\,N\,(q, K, tk)\,ev\,q' = (q',\ \mathsf{own\_next}^{\chi}\,N\,ev\,K,\ \mathsf{tk\_next}\,ev\,tk)}
\end{array}\\[3ex]\begin{array}{rcll}
a \in \sym{th.soup}{S^{N,W,\chi}_n\llbracket\Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket} & \iff & \sym{sp.exists}{\exists A, \Phi}.\ \sym{sp.tfree}{\sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T} \land \text{for each thread } t \text{ running } e\text{,} & \\[1ex]
 & & \quad \sym{sp.rel}{e \in \sym{th.Erel}{E[\kappa_L, \chi]^W_n\llbracket A|_t \vdash U_t\rrbracket^{\varnothing}}} & \text{the relation} \\
 & & \quad \sym{sp.fuel}{e \in \sym{sr.FE}{F^{N}_{n}\llbracket \Phi|_t ; tk_t \vdash \sym{fu.rty}{\mathsf{thread}}\ !\ (\infty, 0) \rrbracket}} & \text{fuel} \\
 & & \land\ \sym{sp.own}{\mathsf{consistent}}(a, A, \Phi) & \\[2ex]
A,\ \Phi & & \text{the held ends as } o \mapsto S@x \text{ for the relation and as } o \mapsto S^{f} \text{ for fuel} & \\
A|_t,\ \Phi|_t & & \text{their restrictions to the ends } K \text{ gives } t & \sym{sp.ty}{U_t \in \{T, \ast\}} \\[2ex]
\sym{sp.own}{\mathsf{consistent}}(a, A, \Phi) & \iff & \sym{sp.dom}{\mathrm{dom}\,A = \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi = \mathrm{dom}\,K} \land \sym{sp.owner}{K(o) = (t, x, f) \Rightarrow t \in \mathrm{dom}\,q} & \text{owners} \\
 & \land & \sym{sp.pts}{K(o) = (t, x, f) \Rightarrow A(o) = \_@x \land \Phi(o) = \_^{f}} \land \sym{sp.fin}{f \in \mathbb{N}} & \\
 & \land & \sym{sp.closed}{o \in \mathrm{dom}\,K \Rightarrow \sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o \in C \lor o \in \mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma} \land \sym{sp.pair}{o \in \mathrm{dom}\,K \land \sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o \in C \Rightarrow \overline{o} \in \mathrm{dom}\,K} & \text{closed} \\
 & \land & \sym{sp.sdual}{\sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o \in C \land A(o) = S@x \land A(\overline{o}) = S'@x' \Rightarrow x' = \overline{x} \land \sym{sty.sdual}{\mathsf{sdual}}\,S\,S'} & \text{dual} \\
 & \land & \sym{sp.pdual}{\sym{end.ech}{\mathsf{ech}}\,o \in C \land \Phi(o) = P^{f} \land \Phi(\overline{o}) = P'^{f'} \Rightarrow P' \mathrel{\sym{sty.sequiv}{\simeq}} \overline{P}} & \\
 & \land & \sym{sp.sig}{\Sigma(o) = S@x \Rightarrow A(o) = S@x} \land \sym{sp.psig}{\Phi(o) = S^{f}} & \text{interface}
\end{array}\end{array}
blocks.caption: An annotated configuration $a = (q, K, tk)$ is a configuration $q$ with an ownership map $K$ and a ticket count per thread. $K$ gives each held end the thread that holds it, its point and its counter. The configuration is in the lock-free process relation at level $n$ when each thread is in $E[\kappa_L]$ at the ends it owns and has fuel at their counters. $A$ and $\Phi$ describe the held ends for the relation and for fuel, and $\mathsf{consistent}$ requires $A$, $\Phi$ and $K$ to agree. Fuel occurs only in this definition.
blocks.why: The lock-free process relation combines the relation and the fuel of each thread over one ownership map, fixed for all levels. Lock-free adequacy reads the points and counters that $K$ records.

deviations.reason: Plain new, with position and facts in its type and worlds that grow, is planned (.claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 2). The Rocq creates with new_ℓ at generated roots of families with laws Λ_ℓ fixed in the world, and with new_κ at a field. The creation choice χ is a proposal of 2026-11-20.

blocks.title: Semantic judgments
blocks.caption: The semantic judgments quantify over levels, larger worlds and substitutions, and read the static future at each of its denotations. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free judgment fixes the counter bound and the annotated configuration once, for all levels.}
blocks.why: The fundamental theorems conclude the semantic judgments, and adequacy takes a semantic judgment as its premise.

sections.title: Theorems
sections.intro: Typed closed processes are deadlock free, and the proof goes through the logical relation. The section opens with the chain of results and then states each of them for processes. The lemmas about terms come last. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free results sit next to their deadlock-free counterparts.}

blocks.title: How the results fit together
blocks.caption: Typing implies the semantic judgment, and the semantic judgment implies deadlock freedom. Both steps use the relation $(V, E, P)$ at the step costs $\kappa_{DF}$. \inmode{lf}{Lock freedom uses the same relation at $\kappa_L$, which excludes internal divergence, together with fuel. The lock-free process relation combines both for each thread. Lock-free adequacy measures a wait on $o$ by $\mu(t) = (\sum_s tk_s, f)$, where $f$ is the counter of $\overline{o}$. A step of the thread holding $\overline{o}$ on another end decreases $f$, which F-Count keeps at $1$ or more. \inmode{lf}{A link uses one ticket.} The thread holding $\overline{o}$ therefore acts on $\overline{o}$ after finitely many steps.}
blocks.why: Each arrow is one theorem of this section. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free rows show what lock freedom adds to the deadlock-free proof.}

blocks.title: Soundness
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{th.soundness}{\begin{array}{l}\varnothing \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.df}{\mathsf{deadlock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-soundness}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.wfworld}{\mathsf{wfworld}}\,W \land \varnothing \sym{tp.lfjudg}{\Vdash^{N}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A closed typed process is deadlock free in a strict world. \inmode{lf}{A closed process typed at a finite counter bound, with each thread guarded, is lock free in a strict and well-founded world.}
blocks.why: These are the main results.

blocks.title: Semantic composition rules
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{th.sem-p-term}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}\sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \land \sym{th.sth}{\mathsf{sth}\,\Theta\,\Sigma\,\Theta_B\,C} \\ \land\ t \in \sym{th.Erel}{E\inmode{lf}{[\kappa]}^{W}_{n}\llbracket \Theta \vdash T\rrbracket^{\varnothing}}\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ (C, \{t\}) \in \sym{th.Prel}{P\inmode{lf}{[\kappa]}^{W}_{n}\llbracket \Sigma \vdash T\rrbracket}\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.sem-p-connect}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}\sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \land \sym{th.conn}{\mathsf{conn}} \\ \land\ p_1 \in \sym{th.Prel}{P^{W_1}_{n}\llbracket \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C \vdash T\rrbracket} \\ \land\ p_2 \in \sym{th.Prel}{P^{W_2}_{n}\llbracket \Sigma_2 \cup \Sigma_D \vdash \ast\rrbracket}\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{th.par}{p_1 \parallel_{\Sigma_C} p_2} \in \sym{th.Prel}{P^{W_1 \mathbin{\sym{w.join}{\sqcup}} W_2}_{n}\llbracket \Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2 \vdash T\rrbracket}\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-p-term}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \Sigma \mathrel{\sym{tp.lfjudg}{\Vdash}}^{N}_{W} (C_0, \{t\}) : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \mathrel{\sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash}}_W (C_0, \{t\}) : T\end{array}}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A safe thread is a safe process, and two safe processes connected at dual interfaces form a safe process. A component proved safe without typing therefore composes with typed components. \inmode{lf}{The same holds for the lock-free process relation.}
blocks.why: P-Term and P-Connect hold in the relation, which makes the approach compositional.

blocks.title: Fundamental theorem
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\sym{th.fundamental-proc}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma \sym{tp.pjudg}{\vdash\inmode{lf}{^{\infty}}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \sym{sj.proc}{\vDash}_W p : T\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\Sigma \sym{tp.lfjudg}{\Vdash^{N}_W} p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Sigma \sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash}_W p : T\end{array}}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A typed process is in the semantic judgment. The proof is by induction over P-Term and P-Connect and uses the composition rules.
blocks.why: The fundamental theorem connects typing with the relation.

blocks.title: Adequacy
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.adequacy}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \varnothing \sym{sj.proc}{\vDash}_W p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.df}{\mathsf{deadlock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}\end{array}\inmodeplain{lf}{\\[3ex]}\inmode{lf}{\begin{array}{l}\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-adequacy}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \sym{th.wfworld}{\mathsf{wfworld}}\,W \land \varnothing \sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash}_W p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}\,p\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-thread-progress}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \sym{th.wfworld}{\mathsf{wfworld}}\,W \land \varnothing \mathrel{\sym{sp.lfsem}{\Vvdash}}_W p : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \begin{array}{l}\forall (r, l).\ \sym{proc.erase}{\mathsf{erase}}\,(\sym{se.run}{r\,0}) = p \land \sym{prop.maximal}{\mathsf{maximal}}\,(r, l) \land \sym{prop.wfair}{\mathsf{wfair}}\,(r, l) \\ \quad \Longrightarrow\ \sym{th.tpr}{\mathsf{thread\_progress\_run}}\,(r, l)\end{array}\end{array}}}\end{array}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: In a strict world, a closed process in the semantic judgment is deadlock free. \inmode{lf}{In a strict and well-founded world, a closed process in the lock-free judgment is lock free, and each thread progresses on each weakly fair maximal run.}
blocks.why: Adequacy connects the relation with the safety property.

blocks.title: Conservativity
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{l}\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.conservative}{\begin{array}{l}(\exists \varepsilon.\ \Gamma;\sym{th.df}{\Delta_{df}} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,\infty}} e : T_{df}\ !\ \varepsilon) \\ \quad\iff\ \Gamma ; \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} e : T_{df}\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.typed-dftyped}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Gamma ; \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_W e : T_{df}\end{array}}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: The annotated judgment at $N = \infty$ types the same terms as deadlock-free typing, and erasing the annotations of a lock-free typing gives a deadlock-free typing.
blocks.why: Lock-free typing therefore rejects no deadlock-free program.

blocks.title: Lemmas about terms
blocks.formula: \begin{array}{c}\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.soundness-source}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \land \varnothing ; \varnothing \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\varnothing}_W t : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.df}{\mathsf{deadlock\_free}}(\varnothing, \{t\})\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.lf-soundness-source}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \sym{th.wfworld}{\mathsf{wfworld}}\,W \land N \in \mathbb{N} \land \sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \\ \land\ \varnothing ; \varnothing \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\varnothing}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ (c, \vartheta) \land \sym{ann.fin0}{\vartheta(0) \in \mathbb{N}} \land \sym{guard.judg}{\varnothing \vdash\!\triangleright t}\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{prop.lf}{\mathsf{lock\_free}}(\varnothing, \{t\})\end{array}}}\end{array}\\[3ex]\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} t : T \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Delta \sym{sj.term}{\mathrel{\sym{sj.proc}{\vDash}}}^{F}_W t : T\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.fundamental-typed}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{th.df}{\Delta_{df}} \mathrel{\sym{sj.term}{\vDash}}^{F}_W t : T_{df}\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.live-fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W} t : T \land \sym{guard.judg}{\varnothing \vdash\!\triangleright t} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Delta \sym{sj.term}{\mathrel{\sym{sj.proc}{\mathrel{|\!\!\vDash}}}}^{F}_W t : T\end{array}}}\inmodeplain{lf}{ \\[1.5ex] }\inmode{lf}{\sym{th.live-fundamental-typed}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}\sym{w.strict}{\mathsf{strict}}\,W \land \varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} t : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \land\ \varnothing \mathrel{\sym{guard.judg}{\vdash\!\triangleright}} t\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \Delta_{df} \mathrel{\sym{sj.term}{\mathrel{|\!\!\vDash}}}^{F}_W t : T_{df}\end{array}}}\end{array}\\[3ex]\sym{th.Erel-bind}{\begin{array}{l}\begin{array}{l}e \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W}_{n}\llbracket \Theta_1 \vdash T\rrbracket^{F \cup \sym{ty.heads}{\mathsf{ap}}\,\Theta_2}} \\ \land\ \forall W' \sym{w.ext}{\sqsupseteq} W,\ j \leq n,\ v \in \sym{th.Vrel}{V^{W'}_j\llbracket\Theta_v \vdash T\rrbracket}. \\ \qquad \sym{se.frame}{f[v]} \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W'}_{j}\llbracket \Theta_v \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}}\end{array} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{se.frame}{f[e]} \in \sym{th.Erel}{E^{W}_{n}\llbracket \Theta_1 \cup \Theta_2 \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}}\end{array}}\inmodeplain{lf}{\\[3ex]}\inmode{lf}{\begin{array}{l}\sym{th.cost-fundamental}{\begin{array}{l}\Gamma ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{F}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{cs.csem}{\Delta \mathrel{\sym{sj.term}{\vDash}}^{N} e : T\ !\ \varepsilon}\end{array}} \\[1.5ex] \sym{th.fsem-of-cost}{\begin{array}{l}\varnothing ; \Delta \mathrel{\sym{tp.vdash}{\vdash}}^{\varnothing}_{W\inmode{lf}{,N}} e : T\ !\ (c, \vartheta) \land \sym{ty.tfree}{\mathsf{tfree}}\,T \land \sym{th.crle}{\mathsf{cr}(\Delta) \leq N} \land \sym{ann.fin0}{\vartheta(0) \in \mathbb{N}} \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\ \sym{fu.fsem}{\mathsf{fsem}\,N\,\sym{th.styof}{\Delta\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}\,e}\end{array}}\end{array}}\end{array}
blocks.caption: A closed program is sound as a one-thread process. Typing a term implies the semantic term judgment, and $E$ is closed under evaluation frames. \inmode{lf}{With the guard a typed term is in the relation at $\kappa_L$, and a typed term at a finite counter bound has fuel.}
blocks.why: The proofs of the process results use these lemmas, each proved rule by rule.

syn.var.title: Variable
syn.var.meaning: A de Bruijn index $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of binders between the occurrence and its binder.
syn.var.why: A plain term former. With de Bruijn indices, substitution $e[v]$ and renaming need no side condition on fresh names.
syn.var.example: $\lambda x.\,x$ is the identity, where $x$ is the index $0$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: A de Bruijn index $x \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of binders between the occurrence and its binder.

syn.unit.title: Unit value $\ast$
syn.unit.meaning: The unit value $\ast$, with $V\llbracket\Theta \vdash \ast\rrbracket$ only at $\Theta = \varnothing$.
syn.unit.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{close}$, $\mathsf{link}$ and $\mathsf{spawn}$ return $\ast$, and a terminated process has $\ast$ in every thread except the main thread.

syn.end.title: End value $o$
syn.end.meaning: The value $o$ names one end of a channel, the only channel name in terms.
syn.end.why: Each end has its own name $c^{+}$ or $c^{-}$, and $\mathsf{select}_i\,o$ and $\mathsf{branch}\,o$ return the same name $o$. Hence no step of the semantics reads a point.
syn.end.example: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ returns the two end values of $c$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: An end $o \in \mathsf{End}$, one of $c^{+}, c^{-}$ for a channel $c$.

syn.lam.title: $\lambda$-abstraction
syn.lam.meaning: A one-argument closure $\lambda e$, a value for every $e$ because no frame has its hole under $\lambda$.
syn.lam.why: A plain term former and the value form of every user function.
syn.lam.example: $\lambda x.\,\mathsf{send}\,x$ is $\mathsf{send}$ as a function value.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, $e \in \mathsf{Expr}$, with the argument as index $0$.

syn.app.title: Application
syn.app.meaning: Application, left to right, with $(\lambda e)\,v \xrightarrow{\beta} e[v]$.
syn.app.why: A plain term former. It is the only way to run a closure, received or built.

args.name: e_2
args.meaning: The argument, evaluated once $e_1$ is a value.

syn.pair.title: Pair
syn.pair.meaning: A pair $\langle e_1, e_2\rangle$, evaluated left to right, a value iff both components are values.
syn.pair.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{send}$ takes a pair $\langle v, o\rangle$ and $\mathsf{recv}$ returns one.

syn.letu.title: Unit elimination
syn.letu.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ \ast = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ evaluates $e_1$ to $\ast$ and then steps to $e_2$ by $\beta$.
syn.letu.why: A plain term former. It sequences $e_1$ before $e_2$ when $e_1$ returns $\ast$, and the derived $\mathsf{let}$ uses it to discard its unit component.

args.name: e_1
args.meaning: A term of type $\ast$, evaluated first.

syn.letp.title: Pair elimination
syn.letp.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ \langle a, b\rangle = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ evaluates $e_1$ to $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle$ and steps to $e_2[v_1, v_2]$ by $\beta$.
syn.letp.why: A plain term former and the only eliminator of $\otimes$. A $\mathsf{recv}$ returns $\langle v, o\rangle$, and the continuation reads $v$ and $o$ through the pair elimination.

args.name: e_1
args.meaning: A term that returns a pair $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle$.

args.name: a, b
args.meaning: The bound variables, $a$ at index $1$ for $v_1$ and $b$ at index $0$ for $v_2$.

args.name: e_2
args.meaning: The body, in scope of $a$ and $b$.

syn.let.title: Derived let
syn.let.meaning: $\mathsf{let}\ a = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2 := \mathsf{let}\ \langle a, u\rangle = \langle e_1, \ast\rangle\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{let}\ \ast = u\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ with $u$ fresh.
syn.let.why: The abbreviation binds one variable without a $\lambda$, so its body keeps every end of the context and the typing needs no lower point $l$ for these ends. It uses only $\otimes$ and $\ast$, which every system already has.
syn.let.breaks: Written as $(\lambda a.\,e_2)\,e_1$ instead, the $\lambda$ must bound the dual points of all ends it captures by one lower point $l$. After $\mathsf{let}\ \langle a, a'\rangle = \mathsf{new}_\ell$ the ends $a, a'$ are at $\rho$ and $\overline{\rho}$, which have no common lower bound, and the body does not type.
syn.let.example: $\mathsf{let}\ p = \mathsf{force}\,mk\,\ast\ \mathsf{in}\ e$ keeps every end of the context in $e$.

args.name: a
args.meaning: The bound variable, standing for the value of $e_1$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: A variable not free in $e_2$, bound to the unit component.

syn.inj.title: Injection
syn.inj.meaning: $\mathsf{inj}_i\,e$ for $i \in \{1, 2\}$, a value when $e$ is a value.
syn.inj.why: A plain term former. $\mathsf{branch}\,o$ returns $\mathsf{inj}_i\,o$, and $i$ records which choice arrived.

syn.case.title: Case
syn.case.meaning: $\mathsf{case}\ e\,(a.e_1)\,(a.e_2)$ evaluates $e$ to $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v$ and steps to $e_i[v]$ by $\beta$.
syn.case.why: A plain term former and the only eliminator of $\oplus$. It consumes the result of $\mathsf{branch}$.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The scrutinee, a term that returns $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v$.

args.name: a
args.meaning: The variable bound to $v$ in each branch, index $0$.

syn.box.title: Box $!e$
syn.box.meaning: A recursive thunk value whose body binds the box at index $0$, $\mathsf{force}\,(!e) \xrightarrow{\beta} e[!e]$.
syn.box.why: One former gives recursion and replication. The value relation asks $\Theta = \varnothing$ and $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$ of a box, so copying a box duplicates no end.
syn.box.example: $!(f = \lambda x.\,\mathsf{let}\ \langle v, x'\rangle = \mathsf{recv}\,x\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{force}\,f\,x')$ is a server loop.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, with the box itself as index $0$.

syn.new.title: $\mathsf{new}$
syn.new.meaning: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ for a fresh channel $c$. The typing places $c^{+}$ at a position $\pi$, a fresh root or a field $x\cdot\kappa$, places $c^{-}$ at $\overline{\pi}$, and states a constraint $C$ on both.
syn.new.why: The term names no point. Position and constraint are part of the existential type of $\mathsf{new}$, which the typing derivation chooses. Each ordering of a new channel is therefore available without program syntax.
syn.new.breaks: With the position or the facts in the term, every held end that the facts mention is an argument that $\mathsf{new}$ takes and returns, because ends are linear.

args.name: \pi
args.meaning: The position of $c^{+}$, a fresh root $\rho$ bound by the existential or a field $x\cdot\kappa$.

args.name: C
args.meaning: The facts of the creation, with $\mathsf{strict}(\Gamma \cup C)$.

syn.op.title: Constant $k$
syn.op.meaning: A constant $k$ is a value, and $k\,v$ takes the head step of $k$ on the value $v$.
syn.op.why: The constants are the operations on channels, boxes and threads. Application $k\,e$ evaluates $e$ first, as each application does.

prim.send.title: $\mathsf{send}$
prim.send.why: The label contains the payload $v$. The value relation is exact, $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ for $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta$, so the ends that leave the thread are determined by $v$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action.

args.name: T, m
args.meaning: The payload type and the number $m$ of point variables it binds, instantiated at the fields $x\cdot i$.

prim.recv.title: $\mathsf{recv}$
prim.recv.why: A receive has a step for each value, so it can match the send of the partner whatever value is sent. The session type of $o$ restricts the $v$ the relation considers.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action.

args.name: T, m
args.meaning: The payload type and the number $m$ of point variables it binds, instantiated at the fields $x\cdot i$.

prim.close.title: $\mathsf{close}$
prim.close.meaning: $\mathsf{close}\,o \xrightarrow{o\,\mathsf{end}} \ast$. The process step pairs it with $\mathsf{close}\,\overline{o}$ and removes $\mathsf{ech}\,o$ from $C$.
prim.close.why: A plain constant. A session type ends in $\mathsf{Close}$, and after both closes no thread holds an end of the channel.
prim.close.example: $\mathsf{close}\,c^{+}$ in one thread and $\mathsf{close}\,c^{-}$ in another.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: The session type of the end before the action.

prim.select.title: $\mathsf{select}_i$
prim.select.meaning: $\mathsf{select}_i\,o \xrightarrow{o \lhd i} o$ for $i \in \{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$, where $\mathsf{false}$ selects the first branch.
prim.select.why: The end continues at $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$, a point that depends on $i$. Hence the two branches are ordered independently.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S_0, S_i
args.meaning: The session type before the action and the chosen continuation.

prim.branch.title: $\mathsf{branch}$
prim.branch.why: A plain constant, the partner of $\mathsf{select}_i$. The injection $\mathsf{inj}_i$ passes the chosen $i$ to the program.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the end acted on, also the upper point of the call.

args.name: S_0, S_1, S_2
args.meaning: The session type before the action and the two continuations.

prim.link.title: $\mathsf{link}$
prim.link.meaning: $\mathsf{link}\,\langle o_1, o_2\rangle \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}} \ast$. The process step removes $\mathsf{ech}\,o_1$ and renames every thread by $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2$.
prim.link.why: A link forwards a conversation without relaying messages. \inmode{lf}{It acts on no protocol, so it costs $0$ in both cost tables, and in the fuel layer it uses one link ticket.}

args.name: \overline{S}@\overline{x}
args.meaning: The second, at the dual type and the dual point.

prim.spawn.title: $\mathsf{spawn}$
prim.spawn.meaning: $\mathsf{spawn}\,v \xrightarrow{\mathsf{spawn}\,v} \ast$, and the process starts a thread running $v\,\ast$.
prim.spawn.why: The label contains the thunk $v$. The value relation is exact, so the child holds exactly the ends $\mathsf{fends}(v)$ and the parent keeps the rest.
prim.spawn.example: $\mathsf{spawn}\,(\lambda u.\,\mathsf{let}\ \ast = u\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{close}\,d')$ transfers $d'$ to the child.

args.name: u, l
args.meaning: The upper and lower point of the thunk, arbitrary.

prim.force.title: $\mathsf{force}$
prim.force.why: A plain constant. It is the only use of a box, and a loop calls itself by $\mathsf{force}$ of its own self variable.
prim.force.example: $\mathsf{force}\,f\,\langle a, b\rangle$ runs the loop $f$ again.
prim.force.signature: \mathsf{force} : \Box(\forall\bar\iota\,\bar\alpha.\ C.\ \ast\multimap^{u} U) \multimap^{u[\bar x]} U[\bar s][\bar x]

args.name: \bar\iota, \bar\alpha
args.meaning: The point and session variables of the box.

args.name: u
args.meaning: The upper point of the body, instantiated as the upper point of the call.

args.name: U
args.meaning: The result type of the body.

syn.values.title: Values
syn.values.why: The results of evaluation. A thread that is a value has finished.

end.cend.title: End
end.cend.meaning: An end $o \in \{c^{+}, c^{-}\}$ of a channel $c$, with one entry per end in every environment.
end.cend.why: The two ends have independent names, and $\mathsf{select}$ and $\mathsf{branch}$ return the name they received. Hence an environment entry is determined by the end alone.

end.dual.title: Dual end $\overline{o}$
end.dual.why: A message on $o$ synchronizes with an action on $\overline{o}$. Every two-thread process step pairs an end with its partner.
end.dual.example: A send on $c^{+}$ meets a receive on $c^{-}$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: An end, $\overline{o}$ is the other end of $\mathsf{ech}\,o$.

end.ech.title: Channel of an end
end.ech.why: Restricted sets $C$ and the subjects of an offer are sets of channels, so the rules map ends to channels by $\mathsf{ech}$.

syn.fends.title: $\mathsf{fends}$
syn.fends.meaning: $\mathsf{fends}(e)$ is the finite set of ends that occur in $e$.
syn.fends.why: The value relation asks $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(\lambda e)$ of a closure and $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$ of a box. Hence for $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta$ the ends a send or spawn of $v$ moves are $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, and ownership follows the syntax of values.

args.name: e
args.meaning: A term, $\mathsf{fends}(e)$ is the set of ends occurring in $e$.

syn.fchans.title: $\mathsf{fchans}$
syn.fchans.why: A created channel $c$ must satisfy $c \notin \mathsf{fchans}(e)$ for every thread $e$, or two channels share a name.

proc.proc.title: Process $(C, E)$
proc.proc.meaning: A process is a pair of a finite set $C$ of restricted channels and a finite multiset $E$ of threads.
proc.proc.why: A channel $c \in C$ has both ends inside the process. An end $o$ with $\mathsf{ech}\,o \notin C$ belongs to the interface with the environment.

args.name: E
args.meaning: The threads, a finite multiset of terms.

proc.config.title: Configuration
proc.config.meaning: A configuration $q = (C, M)$ has a finite partial map $M : \mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup e$ from thread identifiers to terms.
proc.config.why: Weak fairness and lock freedom speak about one thread $t$ across a run, so threads have identifiers.

args.name: M
args.meaning: The thread map, $M(i)$ the term of thread $i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M$.

proc.erase.title: $\mathsf{erase}$
proc.erase.meaning: $\mathsf{erase}(C, M) = (C, \{\!|\, M(i) \mid i \in \mathrm{dom}\,M \,|\!\})$ forgets the identifiers.
proc.erase.why: Steps are defined once, on configurations. A process $p$ steps to $p'$ when some $q$ with $\mathsf{erase}(q) = p$ steps to some $q'$ with $\mathsf{erase}(q') = p'$.

args.name: (C, M)
args.meaning: A configuration, $\mathsf{erase}(C, M)$ keeps $C$ and the multiset of the terms $M(i)$.

pt.const.title: Root $a$
pt.const.meaning: A root $a \in A$ of the world $W$, either shared with the environment or added to $W$ by the creation of a channel.
pt.const.why: Every point of a held end has a root in $A$. The facts $\prec_A$ mention only such points.

args.name: a
args.meaning: A root, $a \in A$ for the world $W$ in use.

pt.var.title: Point variable $\iota$
pt.var.meaning: A de Bruijn point variable, bound by $\Box\forall\bar\iota$, by a payload $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ or by the existential of $\mathsf{new}$, and absent from terms.
pt.var.why: No term mentions a point. Types quantify over points instead.
pt.var.example: $\Box\forall \iota\,\kappa\,\zeta.\ C.\ \ast \multimap U$ binds three point variables.

args.name: \iota
args.meaning: A de Bruijn index over points, bound by $\Box\forall\bar\iota$, by a payload $!(\bar\iota.\,T)$ or by the existential of $\mathsf{new}$.

pt.shift.title: Shift $x^{+}$
pt.shift.meaning: $x^{+}$ raises the offset of $x$ by $1$, so an action on an end at $x$ moves it to $x^{+}$.
pt.shift.why: For every $W$ and $x$, $x \prec_W x^{+}$. Hence the actions of one end are ordered in program order.
pt.shift.example: After $\mathsf{send}$ at $x$ the end is at $x^{+}$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: A point, $x^{+}$ has the offset of $x$ plus $1$.

pt.field.title: Field $x\cdot\kappa$
pt.field.meaning: $x\cdot\kappa$ is a name below $x$ with offset $0$ and positive polarity, where payloads, branch continuations and channels created at a field are.
pt.field.why: The $j$-th payload end of a message at $x$ is at $x\cdot j$, and the continuation of choice $i$ at $x\cdot\kappa_i$. $\mathsf{new}$ may place a channel at the same fields, so a channel created to be sent is at the field where the message delivers its payload.
pt.field.breaks: With a separate sort of point for created channels, a reply channel created to be sent is away from the payload field, and request and reply programs do not type.
pt.field.example: $\mathsf{new}$ at the position $\rho\cdot 0$ places $d^{+}$ at $\rho\cdot 0$ and $d^{-}$ at $\overline{\rho\cdot 0}$.

pt.dual.title: Dual point $\overline{x}$
pt.dual.meaning: $\overline{x}$ flips the polarity of $x$, and the two ends of a channel are at $x$ and $\overline{x}$.
pt.dual.why: A thread blocked at $u$ that holds an end at $v$ must satisfy $u \prec \overline{v}$, the point of the dual end.

args.name: x
args.meaning: A point, $\overline{x}$ has the opposite polarity.

pt.laws.title: Point laws
pt.laws.meaning: For every $x$ and $\kappa$, $\overline{\overline{x}} = x$, $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa$ and $\overline{x^{+}} = \overline{x}^{+}$.
pt.laws.why: $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa$ makes the payload points $x\cdot j$ of sender and receiver equal, although the two ends are at $x$ and $\overline{x}$.
pt.laws.breaks: If $\overline{x}\cdot\kappa \neq x\cdot\kappa$, the ends of a message are at different points for sender and receiver, and the received value is not in the value relation at its type.

sx.kappai.title: Field of a choice $\kappa_i$
sx.kappai.why: The two continuations of a choice are at distinct fields $x\cdot 0 \neq x\cdot 1$, so facts order them independently.

pt.sel.title: Select continuation
pt.sel.meaning: $\mathsf{sel\_pt}\,x\,i = \overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$, the point of the end after $\mathsf{select}_i$ at $x$.
pt.sel.why: Selecting end and branching end continue at the two sides $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$ and $x\cdot\kappa_i$ of one field.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the selecting end before the step.

pt.bra.title: Branch continuation
pt.bra.meaning: $\mathsf{bra\_pt}\,x\,i = x\cdot\kappa_i$, the point of the end after $\mathsf{branch}$ at $\overline{x}$ receives $i$.
pt.bra.why: It is $\overline{\mathsf{sel\_pt}\,x\,i}$, the dual point of the selecting side.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the selecting partner, the branching end is at $\overline{x}$.

pt.payload.title: Payload fields
pt.payload.meaning: The $j$-th end of a message sent at $x$ is at $x\cdot j$.
pt.payload.why: $\overline{x}\cdot j = x\cdot j$, so sender at $x$ and receiver at $\overline{x}$ compute the same points for the delivered ends.
pt.payload.example: A message on $y$ at $Y$ delivers its end at $Y\cdot 0$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: The point of the carrier end at the send.

args.name: m
args.meaning: The number of point variables the payload binds.

lbl.field.title: Field label $\kappa$
lbl.field.meaning: $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}$ selects the field $x\cdot\kappa$ of a point $x$.
lbl.field.why: Payloads, choices and the position of a new channel use fields. $x\cdot\kappa = x\cdot\kappa'$ iff $\kappa = \kappa'$.
lbl.field.breaks: Two channels created at one field $x\cdot\kappa$ are at the same points $x\cdot\kappa$ and $\overline{x\cdot\kappa}$, so no fact orders one before the other.

link.csub.title: $\mathsf{csub}$
link.csub.meaning: $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2 = \{\overline{o_1} \mapsto o_2,\ o_1 \mapsto \overline{o_2}\}$, the identity elsewhere, applied to every thread after a link.
link.csub.why: After the link, the thread holding $\overline{o_1}$ communicates with the thread holding $\overline{o_2}$, so it holds $o_2$. The map identifies $\overline{o_1}$ with $o_2$, so it is no bijection.
link.csub.example: After $\mathsf{link}\,\langle c^{+}, d^{-}\rangle$ the thread holding $c^{-}$ holds $d^{-}$.

args.name: o_1, o_2
args.meaning: The linked ends, the channel of $o_1$ disappears.

se.slabel.title: Session label $\sigma$
se.slabel.meaning: A label $\sigma$ of a step that acts on an end and synchronizes with a partner thread or with the environment.
se.slabel.why: Session labels are exactly the steps a thread can wait on. Readiness and the obligations of the relation are stated over session labels.
se.slabel.example: $o?v$ and $o\,\mathsf{end}$ are session labels, $\beta$ is none.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The value sent or received, where present.

se.subst.title: Substitution $e[v]$
se.subst.meaning: $e[v]$ is $e$ with the value $v$ for the variable of index $0$, and the other indices lowered by one.
se.subst.why: A plain definition. Application, the two lets, case and force step by substitution.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body, with a free index $0$.

se.frame.title: Frame filling $f[e]$
se.frame.meaning: An evaluation frame $f$ is a term with one hole in evaluation position, and $f[e]$ fills the hole with $e$.
se.frame.why: A plain definition. The frames fix where the next step of a term happens.

args.name: f
args.meaning: An evaluation frame, a term with one hole $\square$ in evaluation position.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The term placed in the hole.

se.upd.title: Map update $M[i \mapsto e]$
se.upd.meaning: $M[i \mapsto e]$ maps $i$ to $e$ and every $j \neq i$ to $M(j)$.

se.echans.title: $\mathsf{echans}(M)$
se.echans.why: A created channel $c$ satisfies $c \notin \mathsf{echans}(M)$, so it differs from every channel a thread mentions.

se.subj.title: Subjects $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma$
se.subj.meaning: $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma$ is the set of channels $\sigma$ acts on, $\{\mathsf{ech}\,o\}$ for an action on $o$ and $\{\mathsf{ech}\,o_1, \mathsf{ech}\,o_2\}$ for a link.
se.subj.why: An offer to the environment requires $\mathsf{subj}\,\sigma \cap C = \varnothing$, so it uses only interface channels.

se.parts.title: Participants $\mathsf{parts}(ev)$
se.parts.meaning: $\mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{sync}_{i,j}\,\sigma) = \{i, j\}$, $\mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{solo}_i\,\alpha\,k) = \mathsf{parts}(\mathsf{offer}_i\,\sigma) = \{i\}$, and $\mathsf{parts}(\bot) = \varnothing$ for a stutter. A spawn names only the parent $i$.
se.parts.why: A thread takes part in a step iff it is in $\mathsf{parts}$ of its event. Weak fairness and lock freedom ask whether $t \in \mathsf{parts}(l_j)$ for some position $j$.

args.name: ev
args.meaning: An event. $\mathsf{parts}(ev)$ is the set of identifiers of the threads that take part in the step of $ev$.

se.reach.title: Reachability $\to^{*}$
se.reach.meaning: $p \to^{*} p'$ when $p$ reaches $p'$ in finitely many $\tau$ steps.
se.reach.why: A plain definition. Deadlock freedom and absence of internal divergence quantify over all $p'$ with $p \to^{*} p'$.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: Processes, $p \to^{*} p'$ iff a finite sequence of $\tau$ steps leads from $p$ to $p'$.

se.acc.title: Accessibility $\mathsf{Acc}$
se.acc.meaning: $\mathsf{Acc}\,R\,q$ holds when every $R$-chain $q = q_0\,R\,q_1\,R \cdots$ is finite, inductively, when $\mathsf{Acc}\,R\,q'$ for every $q'$ with $q\,R\,q'$.
se.acc.why: It states the absence of infinite $R$-chains from $q$ by induction, so proofs consume it by well-founded induction.
se.acc.example: If every administrative chain from $q$ has length at most $2$, then $\mathsf{Acc}\ {\to_{\mathsf{admin}}}\ q$.

args.name: R
args.meaning: A relation on $X$, instantiated with $\to_{\mathsf{admin}}$ on processes.

args.name: q
args.meaning: The start element, instantiated with a process reachable from $p$.

se.r0.title: The run starts at $p$
se.r0.meaning: $r_0$ is the configuration at position $0$ of the run, and $\mathsf{erase}(r_0) = p$ states that forgetting its thread names gives the process $p$.
se.r0.why: Lock freedom is a property of a process, and runs are sequences of configurations, so the run must start at a configuration of $p$. Any naming of the threads of $p$ is allowed.

args.name: r_0
args.meaning: The first configuration of the run, $r$ applied to $0$.

args.name: p
args.meaning: The process whose lock freedom is stated.

se.run.title: Runs $r$ and $l$
se.run.meaning: A run is a pair of sequences, $r_i$ the configuration at position $i$ and $l_i$ the event of the step from $r_i$ to $r_{i+1}$, or none when $r_{i+1} = r_i$ stutters.
se.run.why: Lock freedom quantifies over infinite runs and speaks of positions $i \leq j$ in a run.

args.name: l_i
args.meaning: The event of the step $r_i \to r_{i+1}$, or $\bot$ when $r_{i+1} = r_i$.

lbl.beta.title: $\beta$ label
lbl.beta.meaning: The label of application, unit and pair elimination, case and force.
lbl.beta.why: These steps have the same cost $\kappa(\beta)$ in each cost table, so one label covers these steps.

lbl.new.title: Label $\mathsf{new}\,c$
lbl.new.meaning: It contains the name $c$ of the new channel.
lbl.new.why: The process rule reads $c$ to keep names fresh. Position and facts of $c$ are no part of the label, and the relation chooses position and facts.

args.name: c
args.meaning: The name of the new channel.

lbl.spawn.title: Label $\mathsf{spawn}\,v$
lbl.spawn.meaning: It contains the thunk $v$ that starts the child thread $v\,\ast$.
lbl.spawn.why: The relation splits the environment of the parent as $\Theta = \Theta_c \uplus \Theta_r$ with $v$ in the thunk relation at $\Theta_c$. Exactness of $V$ gives $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_c = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the split is determined by $v$.

args.name: v
args.meaning: The thunk, the child thread is $v\,\ast$.

lbl.send.title: Send label $o!v$
lbl.send.meaning: An offer to send the value $v$ on the end $o$.
lbl.send.why: The relation, the fuel layer and scope extrusion read the ends that leave as $\mathsf{fends}(v)$. For $v$ in $V$ at $\Theta_v$ this set is $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_v$.
lbl.send.example: Sending the end $a$ on $o$ has the label $o!a$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.recv.title: Receive label $o?v$
lbl.recv.meaning: An offer to receive $v$ on $o$, for every value $v$.
lbl.recv.why: A receive must meet every send of a partner, so its labels range over all values.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.close.title: Close label $o\,\mathsf{end}$
lbl.close.why: A plain label. Its obligation removes $o$ from the environment $\Theta$, so after a close $o \notin \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.sel.title: Select label $o \lhd i$
lbl.sel.meaning: An offer to select branch $i$ on $o$.
lbl.sel.why: A plain label. Its obligation moves $o$ from $x$ to $\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.bra.title: Branch label $o \rhd i$
lbl.bra.meaning: An offer to receive the choice $i$ on $o$, for both $i$.
lbl.bra.why: A plain label. $\mathsf{branch}$ must meet either choice of the partner, so it has a step for each $i$, and the obligation moves $o$ to $x\cdot\kappa_i$.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end the offer acts on, $o \in \mathsf{End}$.

lbl.link.title: Link label $\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}$
lbl.link.meaning: An unordered pair $\{o_1, o_2\}$ of ends, possibly with $o_1 = o_2$.
lbl.link.why: The label is a set, so one process rule removes the channel of either end.

args.name: o_1, o_2
args.meaning: The linked ends, an unordered pair.

T-Act-App.title: T-Act-App
T-Act-App.why: Call by value. The argument is a value before the body runs.

T-Act-Force.title: T-Act-Force
T-Act-Force.meaning: $\mathsf{force}\,(!e) \xrightarrow{\beta} e[!e]$, so the body runs with the box for its self.
T-Act-Force.why: It is the only rule that unrolls a definition, so recursion and replication go through force steps.

args.name: e
args.meaning: The body of the box, substituted with the box itself.

T-Act-New.title: T-Act-New
T-Act-New.meaning: $\mathsf{new} \xrightarrow{\mathsf{new}\,c} \langle c^{+}, c^{-}\rangle$ for every $c$, and the process rule picks $c$.
T-Act-New.why: The step of a single thread cannot determine which channel names are in use. The process rule asks $c \notin C \cup \mathsf{echans}(M)$.

args.name: c
args.meaning: Any channel name, restricted by the process rule.

T-Act-Spawn.title: T-Act-Spawn
T-Act-Spawn.why: The label contains $v$, so the process rule can start the thread $v\,\ast$.

T-Act-Send.title: T-Act-Send
T-Act-Send.why: The label contains the payload $v$, which the receiving thread obtains by the process rule.

T-Act-Recv.title: T-Act-Recv
T-Act-Recv.why: The step of a single thread does not depend on what the partner sends, so it has a step for each $v$. The receive obligation quantifies only over $v$ in the value relation at the payload type.

args.name: v
args.meaning: Any value, one step for each.

T-Act-Close.title: T-Act-Close
T-Act-Close.why: A plain rule. The process rule pairs it with $\overline{o}\,\mathsf{end}$ in another thread.

T-Act-Select.title: T-Act-Select
T-Act-Select.meaning: $\mathsf{select}_i\,o \xrightarrow{o \lhd i} o$, returning the same end name.
T-Act-Select.why: The end keeps its name $o$, so no step reads a point.

args.name: o
args.meaning: The end, returned under the same name.

T-Act-Branch.title: T-Act-Branch
T-Act-Branch.why: Either choice may arrive, so the thread has one step for each $i$.

args.name: i
args.meaning: The received choice, one step for each $i$.

T-Act-Link.title: T-Act-Link
T-Act-Link.meaning: $\mathsf{link}\,\langle o_1, o_2\rangle \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow\{o_1, o_2\}} \ast$. The label is a set, so $\langle o_1, o_2\rangle$ and $\langle o_2, o_1\rangle$ give one label.
T-Act-Link.why: The renaming $\mathsf{csub}\,o_1\,o_2$ concerns other threads, so the process rule performs the renaming.

T-Act-Ctx.title: T-Act-Ctx
T-Act-Ctx.why: No frame has its hole under $\lambda$ or $!$, so the bodies of closures and boxes take no step before they are called.

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: The term in the hole before and after the step.

args.name: f
args.meaning: An evaluation frame whose subterms left of the hole are values.

sem.frameval.title: $\mathsf{frame\_val}$
sem.frameval.meaning: $\mathsf{frame\_val}\,f$ holds when every subterm of $f$ left of the hole is a value.
sem.frameval.why: It fixes left-to-right evaluation, so every term has at most one redex position.

args.name: f
args.meaning: A frame, $\mathsf{frame\_val}\,f$ iff every subterm of $f$ left of the hole is a value.

P-Act-Beta.title: P-Act-Beta
P-Act-Beta.meaning: If $M(i) \xrightarrow{\beta} e'$, then $(C, M) \to (C, M[i \mapsto e'])$ with event $\mathsf{solo}_i\,\beta\,\cdot$.
