E-Box.body.meaning: The body is typed with no end, the fresh point variables $\bar\iota$, the hypothesis $C(\bar\iota)$, the box as $f$, and the future $(\varnothing, \varphi)$.
E-Box.body.why: Each force instantiates $\bar\iota$ and the session variables anew. The body may assume only $C(\bar\iota)$ and $u \prec \varphi$.
E-Box.body.example: The body of the client loop.
E-Box.body.signature: \Gamma, C(\bar\iota), u \prec \varphi ; \Delta, f \vdash^{(\varnothing, \varphi)} e : U[\bar s]\ !\ \varepsilon

args.name: \bar\iota
args.meaning: the fresh point variables of the box

args.name: \varphi
args.meaning: the future variable of the body

E-Box.open.title: Opened constraint
E-Box.open.meaning: $\Gamma$ extended by the instance $C(\bar\iota)$ at the fresh variables.
E-Box.open.why: The body relies on $C$ at its own point variables, and every force checks $C$ at the chosen instance.
E-Box.open.breaks: Without $C$ the client loop cannot order the points of two consecutive rounds.

args.name: C(\bar\iota)
args.meaning: the constraint at the fresh variables

E-Box.self.title: The self
E-Box.self.meaning: The body binds the box as $f$ at index $0$, at its own type.
E-Box.self.why: This is recursion. \inmode{lf}{A box holds no end, so it has no credit.}

args.name: f
args.meaning: the variable at index $0$ bound to the box itself

E-Force.hold.title: The instance meets $C$
E-Force.hold.meaning: $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$, for points $\bar x$, one per variable of $\bar\iota$.
E-Force.hold.why: The body was typed under $C(\bar\iota)$. Running it at $\bar x$ is correct only when $C[\bar x]$ holds.

args.name: \bar x
args.meaning: the points the force or pack instantiates $\bar\iota$ with, one per variable

E-Force.ub.title: $u[\bar x] \prec F$
E-Force.ub.meaning: The highest point the body waits at, $u$ with the chosen points put in, lies below every point of the future $F$.
E-Force.ub.why: After the force returns, the caller still acts at the points of $F$. If the body waited at a point above one of them, a partner could wait on the caller while the caller waits inside the body. This is the condition $u \prec F$ of E-App for a box.
E-Force.ub.example: The self call of a loop at $\zeta$ under $F = \varnothing$.

args.name: u[\bar x]
args.meaning: the upper point of the box at the instance $\bar x$

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, the points at which the context acts after the term

E-Send.unfold.title: Send head
E-Send.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S_0$ after unfolding, so a recursive protocol $\mu\alpha.S$ needs no rule of its own.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Send.heads.title: $x \prec T$, the action point below a held value
E-Send.heads.meaning: $x \prec T$ states $\Gamma \vdash x \prec y$ for every $y \in \mathsf{ap}(T)$. If $T$ holds hidden ends, $\bot \in \mathsf{ap}(T)$ and the check fails.
E-Send.heads.why: A thread waiting at $x$ while it holds a value of $T$ does not offer the ends in $T$, so readiness asks $x$ below the dual point of each. Hidden ends have no known dual point, so a thread holding them may not wait.
E-Send.heads.breaks: Without $\bot$ in the active points, $\mathsf{send}\,\langle p, o\rangle$ with the unopened pair $p$ of a $\mathsf{new}$ types, and the sender waits while holding ends at points nothing orders.
E-Send.heads.example: The growing ring needs $Y \prec \overline{Y\cdot 0}$ for the payload $a$ of the send on $y$ at $Y$.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of the end the action is on

args.name: T
args.meaning: a held value, in E-Send the payload $T[x\cdot i]$

args.name: y
args.meaning: a dual point of an end in $T$, or $\bot$ for hidden ends, which no $x$ lies below

E-Send.floor.title: One transfer
E-Send.floor.meaning: $T' - 1 \leq T[x\cdot i]$, the payload value aged by one transfer still has the credits the protocol guarantees.
E-Send.floor.why: A transferred end loses $1$ of its counter at the send. Asking the promised credits after the loss bounds how often one end may be transferred.
E-Send.floor.breaks: Without the loss of $1$, an end is transferred forever, and its partner waits forever.
E-Send.floor.example: The growing ring sends $a'$ at credit $4$ against a promised $2$.

args.name: T'
args.meaning: the type of the payload value

args.name: T[x\cdot i]
args.meaning: the payload type of the protocol at the fields of $x$

E-Recv.unfold.title: Receive head
E-Recv.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S_0$ after unfolding, so recursive protocols need no rule of their own.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Close.unfold.title: Close head
E-Close.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S_0$ after unfolding.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Select.unfold.title: Select head
E-Select.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S_0$ after unfolding.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Branch.unfold.title: Branch head
E-Branch.unfold.why: Rules read the first action of $S_0$ after unfolding.

args.name: S_0
args.meaning: the session type of the end before the action

args.name: \mathsf{unfold}
args.meaning: the head normal form, which unfolds $\mu$ and removes leading $\mathsf{Skip}$

E-Link.dual.title: Linked ends dual
E-Link.dual.meaning: $e$ returns $S@x \otimes \overline{S}@\overline{x}$, two ends at dual types and dual points.
E-Link.dual.why: After the link the partners of the two ends form one channel. They are a well-typed pair only when the linked ends are exactly dual at dual points.

args.name: \overline{S}@\overline{x}
args.meaning: the second, at the dual type and dual point

E-SpawnLam.age.title: Transferred ends lose $1$
E-SpawnLam.age.meaning: $\Delta - 1$ lowers the credit of each transferred entry by one.
E-SpawnLam.age.why: A transfer passes each counter minus $1$. A spawn is no action, so this loss is the only bound on how often an end is transferred by spawns.
E-SpawnLam.age.breaks: Under truncation a counter $0$ is transferred as $0$ again, and an end is passed from thread to thread forever.
E-SpawnLam.age.example: In the cycle example the thunk receives $d'$ with credit $1$ less.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the context transferred to the child

E-SpawnLam.body.title: Body of a spawned $\lambda$
E-SpawnLam.body.meaning: $e$ is typed under the transferred $\Delta$ extended by the unit argument, and the empty future.
E-SpawnLam.body.why: A spawned $\lambda$ needs no lower point, because no thread holds it as a closure. Each spawned body therefore gets its own floor.

args.name: \ast
args.meaning: the unit argument of the thunk

E-SpawnLam.future.title: Empty future of the child
E-SpawnLam.future.meaning: The child body runs under $(\varnothing, \cdot)$, a future with no point, no variable and no $\bot$.
E-SpawnLam.future.why: The child is a new thread with no context, so no point of any context lies in its future.
E-SpawnLam.future.breaks: Typing the child under every future above an upper point fails for a body that creates a channel at a fresh root and waits on that channel.

args.name: (\varnothing, \cdot)
args.meaning: the future with no point, no variable and no $\bot$

E-Spawn.credit.title: Closure credit $a \geq 1$
E-Spawn.credit.meaning: A spawned closure value has credit $a \geq 1$.
E-Spawn.credit.why: Spawning passes on the captured ends with their counters minus $1$. The body was typed at each credit minus $a$, and $a \geq 1$ covers that loss.

args.name: a
args.meaning: the credit of the closure value spawned

E-New.bot.title: Lower bound $\bot$
E-New.bot.meaning: The pair is at a root $\rho$ that no point of the context is related to.
E-New.bot.why: $\exists^{\bot}$ records that the ends of the value are at points without a known lower bound, and $\bot$ propagates into every future that holds the value.

args.name: \bot
args.meaning: the lower bound of the existential, no point of the context lies below its ends

E-New.facts.title: The constraint $C$
E-New.facts.meaning: A set of facts, possibly infinite, over $\pi$, its shifts and fields, and points of $\Gamma$.
E-New.facts.why: The derivation chooses the facts the new channel needs, and an interval $l \prec \pi \prec u$ is the simplest case. Opening the existential adds $C$ to $\Gamma$.
E-New.facts.breaks: With facts limited to finitely many bounds by held ends, a client and server loop that orders the two channels at every round, $\iota^{+k} \prec \overline{\kappa^{+k}}$ for all $k$, does not type.

args.name: C
args.meaning: the facts of the creation, chosen by the derivation

E-New.pos.title: Position $\pi$
E-New.pos.meaning: Either $\pi = \rho$, bound by the existential, or $\pi = x\cdot\kappa$ for a point $x$ of the context.
E-New.pos.why: A channel created to be sent on an end at $x$ lands at the field $x\cdot j$ where the receiver expects its $j$-th payload end.
E-New.pos.example: $d$ at $\iota\cdot 0$ in the example with a channel between two box arguments.

args.name: \rho
args.meaning: the point variable bound by the existential

args.name: x, \kappa
args.meaning: a point of the context and a field label

E-New.strict.title: $\mathsf{strict}(\Gamma \cup C)$
E-New.strict.meaning: The facts of $\Gamma$, the order $\prec_W$ and $C$ together derive no $x \prec x$.
E-New.strict.why: Every creation grows the world by $C$, and the results ask a strict world. The check keeps every grown world strict.
E-New.strict.breaks: Facts $\overline{\rho} \prec \rho\cdot 0$ and $\rho\cdot 0 \prec \overline{\rho}$ in one $C$ give a cycle, and two threads waiting on each other would both count as ready.

E-New.dual.title: Dual pair at $N$
E-New.dual.meaning: $c^{+}$ has type $S@\pi$ and $c^{-}$ type $\overline{S}@\overline{\pi}$, both\inmode{lf}{ at credit $N$}.
E-New.dual.why: The fuel layer starts both counters of a new channel at $N$\inmode{lf}{, and the credits} are lower bounds on these counters.

args.name: S
args.meaning: any session type, chosen by the derivation

E-Sub.cost.title: Effects may rise
E-Sub.cost.why: The cost and the ticket need are upper bounds, so a larger bound is also correct. The branches of a case and closures passed to one parameter have different effects, and the larger bound covers both.

E-Weak.drop.title: Weakening
E-Weak.drop.meaning: $\Delta'$ arises from $\Delta$ by emptying entries of unlimited type only.
E-Weak.drop.why: A linear entry may hold ends that must be used, so only entries of unlimited type are dropped.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the context of the conclusion, with additional unlimited entries

E-Pack.lb.title: Lower bound of a pack
E-Pack.lb.meaning: $l = \bot$, the ends become hidden, or $l \preccurlyeq T[\bar x]$, every head of the packed value lies at or above $l$, where $l = \cdot$ asks that $T[\bar x]$ holds no end.
E-Pack.lb.why: After packing, a holding thread refers to the ends only through $l$, so $l$ must bound the active points of the packed value from below. The value relation at an existential states exactly this bound.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower bound of the existential

E-Open.entry.title: Opened entry
E-Open.entry.why: Opening replaces entry $i$ in place. Variable renaming, used for contraction, maps distinct linear entries to distinct indices, and this needs the opened entry to be linear.

args.name: i
args.meaning: the de Bruijn index of the opened variable

E-Open.body.title: Body after opening
E-Open.body.meaning: $e$ is typed with $C(\bar\iota)$ added to $\Gamma$ and entry $i$ replaced by $T$, under the same future and result.
E-Open.body.why: The fresh variables stand for the unknown witness, and $C$ is the only hypothesis about the witness in the scope. Freshness keeps them out of $F$ and $U$.

args.name: \bar\iota
args.meaning: the fresh point variables of the existential

args.name: U
args.meaning: the result type, which mentions no $\bar\iota$

pfree.title: $\mathsf{pfree}\,\Sigma$
pfree.why: P-Term puts every channel whose two ends the thread holds into $C_0$. Hence an interface never holds both ends of a channel, which the semantic P-Connect needs.
pfree.breaks: No program is lost, because such a channel always moves into $C_0$.
pfree.example: $\Sigma = \{c^{+}, c^{-}\}$ is rejected, and $(\{c\}, \ldots)$ with $\Sigma = \varnothing$ types instead.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S@x$

P-Term.C0.title: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_B = \mathsf{ends}(C_0)$
P-Term.C0.meaning: $o \in \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_B$ iff the channel of $o$ is in $C_0$.
P-Term.C0.why: Every end of the thread is an interface end or an end of a restricted channel, and the second kind is exactly $\Theta_B$.

args.name: \Theta_B
args.meaning: the entries of the restricted ends

args.name: C_0
args.meaning: the restricted channels of the thread

P-Term.disj.title: $\mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma \cap C_0 = \varnothing$
P-Term.disj.meaning: No channel of the interface is restricted.
P-Term.disj.why: Then every end of $\Sigma\inmode{lf}{^{N}} \cup \Theta_B$ lies in exactly one part, and the interface is the environment restricted to the channels outside $C_0$.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S@x$

P-Term.pairs.title: Restricted pairs dual
P-Term.pairs.meaning: For every $c \in C_0$ there are $S$ and $x$ with $\Theta_B(c^{+}) = S@x\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$ and $\Theta_B(c^{-}) = \overline{S}@\overline{x}\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$.
P-Term.pairs.why: A restricted channel has both ends inside the process. They synchronize with each other only, so they need dual types at dual points.

args.name: S, x
args.meaning: the type and point of its positive end

P-Term.typed.title: Thread typing
P-Term.typed.meaning: $t$ is typed under no facts, the interface ends and $\Theta_B$, and the empty future.
P-Term.typed.why: The process judgment has static premises only. Its semantic content comes from the fundamental theorems.

P-Term.future.title: Empty future
P-Term.future.meaning: A thread at top level runs under $(\varnothing, \cdot)$.
P-Term.future.why: A thread has no context, so no point lies in its future.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future of a top-level thread

lf.meets.title: $N \in \mathbb{N} \Rightarrow \vartheta(0) \in \mathbb{N}$
lf.meets.meaning: At a finite counter bound the ticket need of the thread is finite, trivial at $N = \infty$.
lf.meets.why: Lock freedom needs a finite number of link tickets per thread, and typing at a finite $N$ does not give one, because a ticket need may have offset $\infty$.
lf.meets.breaks: A loop that links once per round has no finite ticket need and is rejected at finite $N$.
lf.meets.example: $\vartheta = \hat 1$, need $0$, in the examples without links.

args.name: \vartheta
args.meaning: the ticket need of the thread, read at reserve $0$

lf.N.title: $N \in \mathbb{N}$
lf.N.meaning: The counter bound of lock-free typing is a natural number.
lf.N.why: Lock freedom ranks waiting threads by counters as natural numbers, and at $N = \infty$ every counter is $\infty$.

P-Connect.left.title: Left component
P-Connect.left.meaning: $(C_1, E_1)$ is typed over $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_C$ in $W_1$ at result $T$.
P-Connect.left.why: The main thread lies on the left, so the left side has the result $T$ and the right side returns $\ast$.

args.name: \Sigma_C
args.meaning: the cut, the ends connected to the right component

P-Connect.right.title: Right component at $\ast$
P-Connect.right.meaning: $(C_2, E_2)$ is typed over $\Sigma_2 \cup \overline{\Sigma_C}$ in $W_2$ at result $\ast$.
P-Connect.right.why: Only the main thread returns a value, and every other thread returns $\ast$.

P-Connect.cut.title: Exact dual cut $\overline{\Sigma_C}$
P-Connect.cut.meaning: $\overline{\Sigma_C}$ maps $\overline{o}$ to $\overline{S}@\overline{x}$ for every $o \mapsto S@x$ in $\Sigma_C$.
P-Connect.cut.why: After composition the two ends of each cut channel are restricted, and lock freedom asks their protocols dual up to annotations. An exact dual gives this, a dual up to annotations does not.
P-Connect.cut.breaks: \inmode{lf}{An annotation mismatch on a cut channel breaks the payload credit of a later message.}

P-Connect.disj.title: Disjoint channels
P-Connect.disj.meaning: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma_1 \cap \mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma_C = \varnothing$, $\mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma_2 \cap \mathrm{dom}\,\overline{\Sigma_C} = \varnothing$, the channel sets of $\Sigma_1$, $\Sigma_2$, $\Sigma_C$ are pairwise disjoint, $C_1 \cap C_2 = \varnothing$, and each $C_i$ is disjoint from the channels of $\Sigma_1$, $\Sigma_2$, $\Sigma_C$.
P-Connect.disj.why: Every channel then belongs to one side. The cut $\Sigma_C$ is the only channel set both sides use, so composition merges no two channels.
P-Connect.disj.example: Two closes cut at $c$ with $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \varnothing$ and $C_1 = C_2 = \varnothing$.

args.name: C_1, C_2
args.meaning: the restricted channels of the components

P-Connect.cutfree.title: $\mathsf{pfree}\,\Sigma_C$
P-Connect.cutfree.meaning: The cut holds no partner pair.
P-Connect.cutfree.why: The composite interface stays partner-free, which P-Term establishes for single threads.

P-Connect.strict.title: Only the shared part is compared
P-Connect.strict.meaning: $\mathsf{strict}(W_1|_S \sqcup W_2|_S)$ for $S = A_{W_1} \cap A_{W_2}$, the roots of both worlds. $W|_S$ keeps the facts $x \prec_W y$ derivable in $W$ whose roots lie in $S$.
P-Connect.strict.why: Each side is strict by its own derivation, so the only new cycles a join can create run through shared roots. Checking the orders the two sides induce on those roots is enough, and the join is then strict.
P-Connect.strict.breaks: If $W_1$ derives $\rho \prec \rho\cdot 0$ and $W_2$ derives $\rho\cdot 0 \prec \rho$, the join has a cycle and two threads each wait on the other although each side alone is ready.
P-Connect.strict.example: Two worlds without a common root need no check.

args.name: W|_S
args.meaning: the facts of $\prec_W$ between points with roots in $S$

P-Term.strict.title: $\mathsf{strict}\,W$
P-Term.strict.meaning: The world of a single thread is well formed and acyclic.
P-Term.strict.why: Every process derivation then is over a strict world. P-Connect checks only the shared part, and the joined world is strict again.
P-Term.strict.breaks: Without it P-Connect would have to check the whole join.

P-Connect.join.title: Result in $W_1 \sqcup W_2$
P-Connect.join.meaning: The composite is typed in the join of the two worlds.
P-Connect.join.why: Each component keeps its own facts, and the join contains the facts of both.
P-Connect.join.example: Two closes are typed in the join of their two worlds.

guard.judg.title: The guard $\varnothing \vdash\!\triangleright t$
guard.judg.meaning: $\Lambda \vdash\!\triangleright t$ holds iff the self of every box in $t$ is used only after a session action of the body.
guard.judg.why: $\kappa_L$ makes $\beta$ free, so without the guard $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ types and diverges on free steps. Deadlock-free typing does not use the guard.
guard.judg.breaks: $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$ types and is in no relation at $kappa_L$.

args.name: \Lambda
args.meaning: the marks, a list mapping each variable to $\mathsf{true}$ (unusable) or $\mathsf{false}$

guard.marks.title: Marks $\Lambda$
guard.marks.meaning: $\Lambda$ maps each variable to $\mathsf{true}$, marked and not usable, or $\mathsf{false}$.
guard.marks.why: A marked variable denotes a self that is available only one step later, as in guarded recursion.
guard.marks.example: $\mathsf{true}.\varnothing$ marks the self of a box.

args.name: \Lambda(y)
args.meaning: the mark of variable $y$, $\mathsf{true}$ for the self of an enclosing box not yet passed by an action

guard.var.title: Marked variables unusable
guard.var.why: Using the self before an action would recurse with no step of positive cost in between.
guard.var.breaks: $!(f = \lambda x.\,(\mathsf{force}\,f)\,x)$ uses $f$ under a $\lambda$ before any action and is rejected.

args.name: \Lambda
args.meaning: the marks, a list mapping each variable to $\mathsf{true}$ (unusable) or $\mathsf{false}$

guard.lam.title: $\lambda$ keeps the marks
guard.lam.why: The body of a $\lambda$ runs at the level at which the $\lambda$ is a value, so a self marked outside stays marked inside.

args.name: \mathsf{false}.\Lambda
args.meaning: $\Lambda$ with the unmarked argument at index $0$

guard.box.title: A box marks its self
guard.box.why: The self of a box is the recursive call, which must wait for an action.

args.name: \mathsf{true}.\Lambda
args.meaning: $\Lambda$ with the self at index $0$ marked

guard.cong.title: Frames
guard.cong.meaning: A frame checks its first subterm $e_1$ under $\Lambda$ and the rest under the marks $\Lambda'$ that $e_1$ leaves.
guard.cong.why: Without an action no step of positive cost happens, so every mark stays in force until $e_1$ acts.
guard.cong.example: $\Lambda \vdash\!\triangleright e_1\,e_2$ from $\Lambda \vdash\!\triangleright e_1$ and $\Lambda \vdash\!\triangleright e_2$ with $\Lambda' = \Lambda$.

args.name: \Lambda
args.meaning: the marks, a list mapping each variable to $\mathsf{true}$ (unusable) or $\mathsf{false}$

guard.tick.title: $\mathsf{kmarks}\,\Lambda\,\Lambda'\,e$
guard.tick.why: After a session action the rest runs one level lower, where every self is available.
guard.tick.breaks: Without the second case no loop that recurses after an action is guarded.

args.name: \Lambda
args.meaning: the marks, a list mapping each variable to $\mathsf{true}$ (unusable) or $\mathsf{false}$

guard.bind.title: Bound variables unmarked
guard.bind.meaning: Variables bound by a pair elimination or a case are marked $\mathsf{false}$.
guard.bind.why: The bound value is computed by $e_1$ under $\Lambda$. A value checked under $\Lambda$ contains no variable marked in $\Lambda$, so binding it unmarked lets no self escape.
guard.bind.example: $\mathsf{let}\ \langle a, b\rangle = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$ checks $e_2$ under $\mathsf{false}.\mathsf{false}.\Lambda$.

args.name: e_2
args.meaning: the body, with the two bound variables unmarked

args.name: \Lambda'
args.meaning: the marks after the bound term

guard.acts.title: $\mathsf{acts}\,e$
guard.acts.meaning: $\mathsf{acts}$ is the least predicate closed under the clauses shown, so every evaluation of $e$ to a value performs a step $k\,v$ with $k \in \{\mathsf{send}, \mathsf{recv}, \mathsf{close}, \mathsf{select}_i, \mathsf{branch}\}$.
guard.acts.why: Each such step costs at least one level in the live cost table, so the rest after an acting $e_1$ runs one level lower, where the selves are in $V$.

guard.proc.title: Guard of a process $\vdash\!\triangleright p$
guard.proc.why: Live soundness and lock-free typing ask it beside process typing.
guard.proc.example: The client and server main is guarded.

args.name: p
args.meaning: the process $(C, E)$, restricted channels $C$ and a multiset $E$ of threads

tp.Sigma.title: The interface $\Sigma$
tp.Sigma.meaning: $\Sigma$ is a finite map from the ends a process offers to its environment to pairs $S@x$ of a session type and a point.
tp.Sigma.why: A process is typed against its interface, and composition cuts interface ends against each other.

args.name: o
args.meaning: an end offered to the environment

tp.pjudg.title: $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}_{W} p : T$
tp.pjudg.meaning: The process $p$ is typed over $\Sigma$ in $W$ at counter bound $N$ with result $T$, derived by P-Term and P-Connect.
tp.pjudg.why: One judgment serves deadlock freedom at $N = \infty$ and lock freedom at finite $N$.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S@x$

args.name: W
args.meaning: the world whose order $\prec_W$ the rule reads

args.name: p
args.meaning: the process $(C, E)$, restricted channels $C$ and a multiset $E$ of threads

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

tp.lfjudg.title: $\Sigma \Vdash^{N}_{W} p : T$
tp.lfjudg.meaning: $\Sigma \Vdash^{N}_{W} p : T$ iff $N \in \mathbb{N}$, $\Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}_{W} p : T$ and $\vdash\!\triangleright p$.
tp.lfjudg.why: Lock freedom needs finite counters and no infinite run of free steps, and the guard excludes the latter.
tp.lfjudg.example: Two threads closing $c^{+}$ and $c^{-}$, at every $N \in \mathbb{N}$.
tp.lfjudg.signature: \Sigma \Vdash^{N}_{W} p : T \iff N \in \mathbb{N} \land \Sigma \vdash\inmode{lf}{\inmode{lf}{^{N}}}_{W} p : T \land \vdash\!\triangleright p

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S@x$

args.name: W
args.meaning: the world whose order $\prec_W$ the rule reads

args.name: p
args.meaning: the process $(C, E)$, restricted channels $C$ and a multiset $E$ of threads

args.name: T
args.meaning: the result type of the main thread

tp.chans.title: $\mathsf{chans}\,\Sigma$
tp.chans.meaning: The set of channels of the ends in $\mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma$.
tp.chans.why: Restricted sets are sets of channels, so disjointness is stated on channels.

tp.ends.title: $\mathsf{ends}(C)$
tp.ends.why: A restricted channel contributes both its ends.

tp.lift.title: $\Sigma\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$
tp.lift.why: Interface ends start a thread\inmode{lf}{ at credit $N$}, as fresh ends do.

args.name: \Sigma
args.meaning: the interface, a finite map from the ends the process offers to its environment to $S@x$

E-Box.fresh.title: $\bar\iota$ fresh
E-Box.fresh.meaning: The bound point variables $\bar\iota$ occur nowhere in $\Gamma$, $\Delta$, $F$ or the result type.
E-Box.fresh.why: They stand for points chosen later, at each force or for the unknown witness of an existential, so nothing in scope may mention these variables. The Rocq uses de Bruijn indices and shifts the context instead.
E-Box.fresh.example: Opening $\exists^{\bot}\iota.\,C.\,T$ under a context that mentions $\rho$ picks $\iota \neq \rho$.

tp.pinst.title: Point instance $T[\bar x]$
tp.pinst.meaning: Replaces the point variables $\bar\iota$ of $T$ by the points $\bar x$.
tp.pinst.why: Forcing and packing choose concrete points for the bound variables.

args.name: T
args.meaning: a type over the bound point variables $\bar\iota$

tp.sinst.title: Session instance $U[\bar s]$
tp.sinst.meaning: Replaces the session variables of $U$ by the session types $\bar s$.
tp.sinst.why: A box is polymorphic in its session variables, and each force chooses an instance.

args.name: U
args.meaning: a type over the session variables $\bar\alpha$

tp.sinsts.title: Allowed session instances $\mathsf{sinsts}\,\bar s$
tp.sinsts.meaning: The session types a session variable of a box may stand for. Every recursion $\mu\alpha.S$ inside each $s \in \bar s$, also inside payloads, passes an action before $\alpha$ recurs. \inmode{lf}{At $N = \infty$ each $s$ also has no finite credit.}
tp.sinsts.why: The rules read the first action of a protocol after unfolding. An instance such as $\mu\alpha.\alpha$ has no first action, so substituting it would give an end no rule can type. \inmode{lf}{At $N = \infty$ every annotation in a derivation is $\infty$, and an instance with a finite credit inside its payloads would bring one in.}
tp.sinsts.breaks: Without the first condition a box with a variable $\alpha$ could be forced at $\mu\alpha.\alpha$, and an end of type $\mu\alpha.\alpha$ would be stuck with no action to perform.
tp.sinsts.example: $\mu\alpha.\,{!}\ast.\alpha$ and $\mathsf{Close}$ are allowed, $\mu\alpha.\alpha$ and $\mu\alpha.\,\mathsf{Skip}.\alpha$ are not.

tp.max.title: $\max(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$
tp.max.meaning: The larger of two effects, $(\max(c_1, c_2), \max(\vartheta_1, \vartheta_2))$ with the ticket needs compared pointwise.
tp.max.why: Only one branch of a case runs, so its effect is bounded by the larger of the two.

args.name: \varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2
args.meaning: the effects of the two branches

tp.vdash.title: The term turnstile $\vdash$
tp.vdash.meaning: The least relation closed under E-Unit to E-Open. The deadlock-free judgment $\Gamma ; \Delta \vdash^{F} t : T$ is the instance $N = \infty$ with every annotation $\infty$.
tp.vdash.why: One relation has the session type, the points and, in the lock-free mode, the\inmode{lf}{ credits and }the effect of $e$, so every mode reads its premises off one derivation.

args.name: \Gamma
args.meaning: the hypotheses, constraint instances $(C, \bar x)$ and future variables $\varphi \mapsto u$

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context, ends $o$ with end types and de Bruijn indices with types

args.name: H
args.meaning: the entries the thread holds while $e$ runs, a context or a type

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, the points at which the context acts after the term

args.name: \varepsilon
args.meaning: \inmode{lf}{the effect of $e$, its cost and ticket need, lock-free mode only}

tp.msunion.title: Multiset union $E_1 \uplus E_2$
tp.msunion.meaning: $E_1 \uplus E_2$, the multiset sum, counts every thread as often as $E_1$ and $E_2$ together.
tp.msunion.why: A composite process runs the threads of both components side by side.

args.name: E_1, E_2
args.meaning: the thread multisets of the two components

ct.table.title: Cost table $\kappa$
ct.table.meaning: A sextuple $\kappa \in \mathbb{N}^6$ of costs, one per kind of step.
ct.table.why: One relation parametric in $\kappa$ yields both the deadlock-freedom and the liveness relation, so each compatibility proof is done once for all $\kappa$.

args.name: \kappa_\beta, \ldots, \kappa_{take}
args.meaning: the costs of $\beta$, creation, spawn, link, give and take

ct.take-pos.title: $1 \leq \kappa_{take}$
ct.take-pos.meaning: Receive and branch cost at least one level.
ct.take-pos.why: A receive reads $V$ of its payload negatively at the level of its continuation, so that level is $j < n$ and $V_n$ is well defined.
ct.take-pos.breaks: With $\kappa_{take} = 0$, $V_n$ would quantify negatively over $V_n$ and the fixpoint would not exist.

ct.give-pos.title: $\kappa_\beta = 0 \Rightarrow 1 \leq \kappa_{give}$
ct.give-pos.meaning: If $\beta$ is free, a give costs at least one level.
ct.give-pos.why: For $\kappa_\beta = 0$, $V_n$ and $E_n$ are defined together by recursion on the size of the type, and a free send would read $V_n$ at a payload type of any size.

ct.give-take.title: $\kappa_{give} \leq \kappa_{take}$
ct.give-take.meaning: A give costs at most a take.
ct.give-take.why: A synchronization costs $\kappa_{give} + \kappa_{take}$, and composing two components counts a synchronization as two gives, which needs $2\kappa_{give} \leq \kappa_{give} + \kappa_{take}$.

ct.DF.title: $\kappa_{DF}$, the step index
ct.DF.meaning: The table $(1,1,1,0,0,1)$. It is the ordinary step index of a logical relation. Almost every step costs one level, and only a send, select, close or link costs none.
ct.DF.why: A step index lets $V$ and $E$ refer to themselves at lower levels, which recursion and received closures need. Each of the four free steps shrinks the term, so the successor is checked at the same level by recursion on the term. A send therefore passes its payload on at the level of the continuation.
ct.DF.example: $\beta$ and $\mathsf{recv}$ cost one level, $\mathsf{send}$ costs none.

ct.L.title: $\kappa_L$, the live table
ct.L.meaning: The table $(0,0,0,0,1,1)$. Internal steps, $\beta$, $\mathsf{new}$, $\mathsf{spawn}$ and $\mathsf{link}$, cost nothing, and only session actions cost a level.
ct.L.why: A free step is checked inside the least fixpoint of the current level, and a least fixpoint admits only finitely many steps in a row. So a term in the relation at $\kappa_L$ cannot take infinitely many internal steps without an action, which is absence of internal divergence. Lock freedom needs it, because a thread that loops internally never serves its partner. It is not about paying for messages.
ct.L.breaks: $!(f = \\mathsf{force}\\,f)$ steps by $\\beta$ forever and is in no level at $\\kappa_L$, while it is in every level at $\\kappa_{DF}$.
ct.L.example: Under $\kappa_L$ a synchronization costs $2$, one level for each side.

ct.beta.title: Cost $\kappa_\beta$
ct.beta.meaning: The cost of application, pair and unit elimination, case and force.
ct.beta.why: An arrow reads its body at every $j < n$ under $\kappa_{DF}$. \inmode{lf}{Under a general table it reads every $j$ with $j + \kappa_\beta \leq n$, so one arrow clause also serves $j \leq n$ for $\kappa_L$.}

ct.new.title: Cost $\kappa_{new}$
ct.new.why: Creation synchronizes with nobody, so $\kappa_L$ counts it as an internal step.

ct.spawn.title: Cost $\kappa_{spawn}$
ct.spawn.why: For $\kappa_{spawn} = 0$ the child thunk is read inside the least fixpoint of the parent, so an infinite chain of spawns is in no $E_n$.

ct.link.title: Cost $\kappa_{link}$
ct.link.meaning: The cost of $\mathsf{link}$, $0$ in both tables.
ct.link.why: A link acts alone and synchronizes with nobody, so it is an internal step.
ct.link.breaks: Under $\kappa_L$ a loop that creates and links forever is an infinite sequence of internal steps and lies in no $E_n$.
ct.link.example: $!(f = \mathsf{let}\ \langle a, b\rangle = \mathsf{new}\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{let}\ \ast = \mathsf{link}\,\langle a, b\rangle\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{force}\,f)$ diverges internally.

ct.give.title: Cost $\kappa_{give}$
ct.give.why: The obligation of a give reads the continuation at level $n - \kappa_{give}$.

ct.takek.title: Cost $\kappa_{take}$
ct.takek.meaning: The cost of $\mathsf{recv}$ and $\mathsf{branch}$, $1$ in both tables.
ct.takek.why: The obligation of a take reads every incoming value at $j \leq n - \kappa_{take} < n$.

ct.sync.title: Cost of an event $\kappa(ev)$
ct.sync.meaning: $\kappa(ev)$ is the cost of the step kind of $ev$, and $\kappa_{give} + \kappa_{take}$ for a synchronization.
ct.sync.why: Both partners of a synchronization step at once, so the step of the process costs the sum of both costs.
ct.sync.example: A message costs $1$ under $\kappa_{DF}$\inmode{lf}{ and $2$ under $\kappa_L$}.

args.name: ev
args.meaning: an event of the instrumented semantics

rel.atcost.title: $e'$ at $\Theta'$
rel.atcost.meaning: The successor of a step of cost $c$ at level $n$ is read in the fixpoint $X$ if $c = 0$ and in $E_{n-c}$ if $c > 0$.
rel.atcost.why: Stated as two implications, $X$ occurs strictly positively and the inductive definition is admissible.
rel.atcost.example: Under $\kappa_L$ a $\beta$ step stays at level $n$.

args.name: \kappa(\alpha)
args.meaning: the cost of the step label $\alpha$

args.name: X
args.meaning: the least fixpoint under construction at level $n$

rel.lfp.title: Least fixpoint $X$
rel.lfp.meaning: $E_n$ and $P_n$ are the least fixpoints of their clauses over steps of cost $0$.
rel.lfp.why: A least fixpoint admits only finite sequences of cost-$0$ steps, so under $\kappa_L$ no term in $E_n$ diverges internally.
rel.lfp.breaks: A greatest fixpoint would admit $!(f = \mathsf{force}\,f)$, which takes only $\beta$ steps.
rel.lfp.example: Induction on $E_n$ is induction on cost-$0$ steps.

args.name: X
args.meaning: the least relation closed under the clauses of level $n$

V-Unit.title: $V$ at $\ast$
V-Unit.why: A finished thread has result type $T$ or $\ast$, and $\Theta = \varnothing$ shows that a thread holding a value of type $\ast$ holds no end.
V-Unit.breaks: Without $\Theta = \varnothing$, a thread could end as $\ast$ while owning an end that its partner waits on forever.

V-Sess.title: $V$ at $S@x$
V-Sess.meaning: $v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash S@x\rrbracket \iff \exists o, S'.\ v = o \land \Theta = \{o \mapsto S'@x\} \land S' \approx S$.
V-Sess.why: $\Theta$ keeps its annotations for the fuel layer, and $V$ compares session types erased.

args.name: S'
args.meaning: the session type of $o$ in $\Theta$, with annotations

V-Sess.exact.title: $\Theta = \{o \mapsto S'@x\}$
V-Sess.exact.meaning: The environment of an end value is the singleton of its own entry at the point $x$ of the type.
V-Sess.exact.why: Exact environments make $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ for every $v \in V$, which fixes ownership at sends and spawns.

args.name: S'@x
args.meaning: the entry of $o$, at the point $x$ of the type

V-Prod.title: $V$ at $\otimes$
V-Prod.meaning: $\langle v_1, v_2\rangle \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_1 \otimes T_2\rrbracket \iff \exists \Theta_1, \Theta_2.\ \Theta = \Theta_1 \uplus \Theta_2 \land \forall i.\ v_i \in V\llbracket\Theta_i \vdash T_i\rrbracket$.
V-Prod.why: The clause mirrors E-Pair, and the disjoint split keeps environments exact through pairs.

args.name: \Theta_1, \Theta_2
args.meaning: the disjoint parts owned by $v_1$ and $v_2$

V-Prod.split.title: $\Theta = \Theta_1 \uplus \Theta_2$
V-Prod.split.meaning: The components own disjoint parts of $\Theta$.
V-Prod.split.why: An end is owned by exactly one component, so no renaming can move a held end into a box inside a pair.

V-Sum.title: $V$ at $\oplus$
V-Sum.meaning: $\mathsf{inj}_i\,v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_1 \oplus T_2\rrbracket \iff v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T_i\rrbracket$.
V-Sum.why: The clause mirrors E-Inj and E-Case, and branch returns its end in an injection.

V-Arrow.exact.title: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(e)$
V-Arrow.exact.meaning: A closure owns exactly the ends its body mentions.
V-Arrow.exact.why: With it, every $v \in V$ satisfies $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the ends a send or spawn passes on are $\mathsf{fends}$ of the value.
V-Arrow.exact.breaks: $\lambda\_.\,\mathsf{let}\ \ast = \Omega\ \mathsf{in}\ \mathsf{close}\,q^{+}$ owns nothing and is in $V$ at every level, and then a send of it next to $q^{+}$ fails E-Send.

V-Arrow.lb.title: $l \preccurlyeq \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta$
V-Arrow.lb.meaning: For $l = y$, $\forall z \in \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta.\ y \preccurlyeq z$, and for $l$ absent, $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \varnothing$.
V-Arrow.lb.why: The thread holding a closure reads its active points through $l$, which bounds the active points of the values it holds.
V-Arrow.lb.example: A closure over $a$ at $\rho$ has $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \{\overline{\rho}\}$ and $l = \overline{\rho}$.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower point of the arrow, a point or absent

V-Arrow.kripke.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
V-Arrow.kripke.meaning: The body is in $E$ in every extension $W'$ of $W$.
V-Arrow.kripke.why: A closure may be called after composition has extended the world, so $V$ is monotone in $W$.
V-Arrow.kripke.example: A received closure is called in $W \sqcup W'$.

V-Arrow.level.title: Level of the body
V-Arrow.level.meaning: The body is read at every level $j < n$, \inmode{lf}{and under a general table at every $j \leq n - \kappa_\beta$.}
V-Arrow.level.why: A $\beta$-step costs one level in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$, where $\beta$ is free, the body is read at level $n$.}
V-Arrow.level.example: The body of a closure in $V_3$ is read at levels $0$ to $2$.

args.name: j
args.meaning: the level at which the body is read

V-Arrow.ub.title: $W' \vdash u \prec F$
V-Arrow.ub.meaning: The body is in $E$ under every future $F$ with $\forall y \in F.\ W' \vdash u \prec y$.
V-Arrow.ub.why: A closure may block up to $u$, so its caller must still act only above $u$.
V-Arrow.ub.example: The body of $\mathsf{between}$ runs under every $F$ above $\kappa$.

args.name: u
args.meaning: the upper point of the arrow, a point or absent

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future of the call, any set of points above $u$

V-Arrow.body.title: Body in $E$
V-Arrow.body.meaning: $e[w] \in E^{W'}_j\llbracket\Theta \cup \Theta' \vdash U\rrbracket^{F}$ for every argument $w \in V^{W'}_j\llbracket\Theta' \vdash T\rrbracket$ with $\Theta' \mathbin{\#} \Theta$.
V-Arrow.body.why: The call owns the closure's ends and the argument's ends, which are disjoint, and the compatibility of E-App feeds exactly this union to the body.
V-Arrow.body.example: $\mathsf{cli}$ applied to $\langle a, b\rangle$ runs at $\{a, b\}$.

args.name: \Theta'
args.meaning: the ends of the argument, disjoint from $\Theta$

FV-Arrow.call.title: $\Phi' \geq \Phi - a$
FV-Arrow.call.meaning: At the call each captured end has the protocol it had at creation and a counter at least its counter at creation minus $a$.
FV-Arrow.call.why: Aging a closure by $c \leq a$ lowers $a$ and the counters by $c$ together, so the difference stays, and the body was typed at each credit minus $a$.
FV-Arrow.call.example: A closure at credit $1$ created with counter $3$ on $o$ is called with counter $2$ or more on $o$.
FV-Arrow.call.signature: \forall o.\ \Phi(o) = S^{f} \Rightarrow \Phi'(o) = S^{f'} \land f' \geq f - a

args.name: \Phi'
args.meaning: the captured ends at the call

deviations.reason: Not yet in the Rocq, see .claude/notes/redesign/pending.md, entry 12.

V-Thunk.empty.title: Empty future $\varnothing$
V-Thunk.empty.meaning: The spawned body is read at $F = \varnothing$ with no lower and no upper point.
V-Thunk.empty.why: The thunk leaves the parent and starts a thread with no context, so no readiness of the parent reads its active points and no code of the parent runs after the thunk in the child.
V-Thunk.empty.breaks: With a lower point, a thread holding ends at unrelated points $1$ and $2$ could not spawn a thunk that closes both.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future of the spawned body

V-Box.empty.title: $\Theta = \varnothing$
V-Box.empty.meaning: A box value owns no end.
V-Box.empty.why: Every value in $V$ satisfies $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, and at a box this is $\Theta = \varnothing$.
V-Box.empty.breaks: Without it, a box could be copied together with an end it owns.

V-Box.noends.title: $\mathsf{fends}(e) = \varnothing$
V-Box.noends.meaning: The body of a box mentions no end.
V-Box.noends.why: A box is unlimited, so it must be copyable, and an end mentioned inside would be copied with the box.
V-Box.noends.breaks: A box hiding an end under an empty environment could be forced twice and act on the end twice.

V-Box.kripke.title: $\forall W' \sqsupseteq W$
V-Box.kripke.meaning: The thunk is in $V$ in every extension $W'$ of $W$.
V-Box.kripke.why: $V$ is monotone in $W$, and at a box the extension cannot be pushed into the thunk clause, because the instances $\bar x$ range over points ordered only in $W'$.
V-Box.kripke.breaks: Without it, a box received after composition could not be forced at an instance whose constraint holds only in the joined world.
V-Box.kripke.example: Forcing a received box in $W \sqcup W'$.

V-Box.inst.title: $W' \vdash C[\bar x]$
V-Box.inst.meaning: The thunk is in $V$ at every instance $\bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^m$ with $\forall (y \prec z) \in C.\ W' \vdash y[\bar x] \prec z[\bar x]$.
V-Box.inst.why: E-Force asks $\Gamma \vdash C[\bar x]$ at its instance, so the box must work at every instance meeting $C$ and at no other.

args.name: C
args.meaning: the box constraint over $m$ point variables

V-Box.hc.title: Hereditarily contractive instances
V-Box.hc.meaning: The thunk is in $V$ at every list $\bar s$ of $k$ hereditarily contractive session types.
V-Box.hc.why: Session instances must unfold to a head, which hereditary contractiveness guarantees.

V-Box.thunk.title: The thunk at level $n$
V-Box.thunk.why: $\mathsf{size}(\Box\ldots) > \mathsf{size}(\ast \multimap U)$, so $V$ at the box reads $V$ at the thunk type inside level $n$.

args.name: u[\bar x]
args.meaning: the upper point instantiated at $\bar x$

args.name: U[\bar s][\bar x]
args.meaning: the result instantiated at $\bar s$ and $\bar x$

V-Ex.lb.title: $l \preccurlyeq \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta$
V-Ex.lb.meaning: For $l = y$, $\forall z \in \mathsf{ap}\,\Theta.\ y \preccurlyeq z$, for $l$ absent $\mathsf{ap}\,\Theta = \varnothing$, and for $l = \bot$ nothing.
V-Ex.lb.why: It lets a holding thread bound the actual active points of a packed value by its static active points, which the readiness of a send carrying a packed payload and the compatibility of E-Pack use.
V-Ex.lb.breaks: Without it, a sender holding a packed payload could not show its offered end below the dual points of the payload ends.

args.name: l
args.meaning: the lower bound, a point, absent or $\bot$

V-Ex.witness.title: A witness in $W$
V-Ex.witness.meaning: $\exists \bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^m.\ W \vdash C[\bar x] \land v \in V\llbracket\Theta \vdash T[\bar x]\rrbracket$.
V-Ex.witness.why: Opening an existential substitutes fresh point variables and adds $C$ to $\Gamma$, and the compatibility of E-Open instantiates them with this witness.
V-Ex.witness.example: The fresh root $a$ with the facts $C$ of its creation.
V-Ex.witness.signature: \exists \bar x \in \mathsf{Point}^{m}.\ W \vdash C[\bar x] \land v \in V^{W}_{n}\llbracket \Theta \vdash T[\bar x] \rrbracket

args.name: T[\bar x]
args.meaning: the body type at the witness

rel.vsize.title: Recursion on $(n, \mathsf{size}\,T)$
rel.vsize.meaning: $V_n$ is defined by recursion on $n$ and, inside a level, on the size of the type, with all levels built by one course-of-values fixpoint.
rel.vsize.why: Under $\kappa_L$, $V_n$ reads $E_n$ and $V_n$ at smaller types, and instantiation preserves size.

E.zero.title: Level $0$
E.zero.why: Step indexing starts from the trivial relation.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

E.kripke.title: $\forall W_1 \sqsupseteq W$
E.kripke.meaning: Each unfolding of $E$ holds in every extension $W_1$ of $W$.
E.kripke.why: $E$ is monotone in $W$ by definition, so no clause needs its own world quantifier.

args.name: W_1
args.meaning: any extension of $W$, the world at which the clauses are read

E.stop.title: (stop)
E.stop.why: A term that takes no step must be a value in $V$, so a stuck term is in no $E_n$ for $n \geq 1$ and adequacy reads termination off $V$.
E.stop.breaks: A stuck non-value would count as well typed, and adequacy would fail.

E.ready.title: (ready)
E.ready.why: Readiness excludes circular waiting between threads.
E.ready.breaks: Two threads each waiting on the partner of the other's second end deadlock.

E.step.title: (step)
E.step.why: One conjunct per kind of label keeps $X$ strictly positive.

O-Beta.title: O-Beta
O-Beta.why: A $\beta$ step changes no end, and the compatibility of every elimination rule discharges it by reading the redex at the same environment.
O-Beta.example: Under $\kappa_L$ a $\beta$ step stays at level $n$.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-New.title: O-New
O-New.meaning: For a fresh name $c$ and every root $a \notin A_W$, some $S$, position $\pi$ and facts $C$ with $\mathsf{strict}(W \oplus C)$ place $c^{+}$ at $S@\pi$ and $c^{-}$ at $\overline{S}@\overline{\pi}$, and the successor runs in $W \oplus C$.
O-New.why: It is the semantic counterpart of E-New. The typing chooses $\pi$ and $C$, and the relation continues in the grown world.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-New.cfresh.title: $c^{\pm} \notin \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta$
O-New.cfresh.meaning: The new name is no end of $\Theta$.
O-New.cfresh.why: The process rule picks $c$ globally fresh, so the term obligation may assume freshness.

O-New.forall.title: For every fresh root
O-New.forall.meaning: The obligation holds at every root $a$ outside $A_W$.
O-New.forall.why: The root is then a function of the run, the same at every level.
O-New.forall.breaks: A root chosen per level breaks lock freedom, because no ownership is then the same at every level.

O-New.gfresh.title: $a \notin A_W$
O-New.gfresh.meaning: The root $a$ is no root of the current world.
O-New.gfresh.why: Roots come from a supply separate from channel names, so a link that renames a channel never revives a used root.

O-New.grow.title: Position and growth
O-New.grow.meaning: $\pi$ is the fresh root $a$ or a field $x\cdot\kappa$, and $C$ is a set of facts over $\pi$ and points of $W$ with $\mathsf{strict}(W \oplus C)$.
O-New.grow.why: The witness of the existential that E-New returns is $\pi$, and the facts it states hold in $W \oplus C$.

args.name: \pi
args.meaning: the position, the root $a$ or a field of a point $x$ of $W$

O-New.dual.title: Dual placement
O-New.dual.why: It is the static result of E-New at the witness $\pi$, and duality of the pair is what the lock-free process relation asks of restricted channels.

O-Spawn.title: O-Spawn
O-Spawn.meaning: $\Theta$ splits into a part $\Theta_M$ for the thunk, which is in $V^{W}_{n}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash \ast \multimap^{\top}_{\bot} \ast\rrbracket$, and a rest $\Theta_r$ for the continuation.
O-Spawn.why: Exactness of $V$ fixes $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_M = \mathsf{fends}(v)$, so the split is the same at every level.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: \Theta_M, \Theta_r
args.meaning: the parts of the child and of the parent

O-Spawn.split.title: $\Theta = \Theta_M \uplus \Theta_r$
O-Spawn.split.meaning: The child and the parent own disjoint parts of $\Theta$.
O-Spawn.split.why: The fundamental theorem builds the split from E-Spawn's split of the context, and the lock-free process relation moves exactly $\Theta_M$ to the new thread.

O-Spawn.transfer.title: $\mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_M = \mathsf{fends}(v)$
O-Spawn.transfer.meaning: The part that leaves is exactly the set of ends of the value that leaves.
O-Spawn.transfer.why: It follows from exactness of $V$, which makes ownership at a transfer independent of the level.
O-Spawn.transfer.breaks: Without exactness, an end mentioned by neither side could go to either side at different levels.

args.name: v
args.meaning: the value that leaves, the thunk or the payload

O-Spawn.thunk.title: $v \in V^{W}_{n}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash \ast \multimap^{\top}_{\bot} \ast\rrbracket$
O-Spawn.thunk.meaning: The thunk is a closure at upper point $\top$ and lower point $\bot$, in $V$ at the parent's level $n$. At $u = \top$ its body is read at the empty future.
O-Spawn.thunk.why: For $\kappa_{spawn} = 0$ the child is read inside the parent's least fixpoint, so an infinite chain of spawns is in no $E_n$.

O-Send.title: O-Send
O-Send.meaning: The subject is at a send head, $\Theta \setminus o$ splits into the payload part $\Theta_M$ and the rest, the payload is in $V$, and the continuation runs at the rest with $o$ at $S@x^{+}$.
O-Send.example: $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ in the growing ring.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: S_0, S
args.meaning: the session type of the subject and its continuation after the head

args.name: m, U, b
args.meaning: the number of point variables, the type\inmode{lf}{ and the credit} of the payload

O-Send.split.title: $\Theta \setminus o = \Theta_M \uplus \Theta_r$
O-Send.split.meaning: The payload owns no copy of the subject $o$.
O-Send.split.why: A send gives away held ends other than its subject.
O-Send.split.breaks: A term that sends its own subject would leave the continuation acting on an end it gave away.

sr.head.title: Head of an end $\Theta(o) \doteq S@x$
sr.head.meaning: $\Theta(o) \doteq S@x$ states $\Theta(o) = S_0@x$ for some $S_0$ with $\mathsf{unfold}\,S_0 = S$.
sr.head.why: Every obligation reads the first action of the subject end after unfolding, so the notation states it once.

args.name: S
args.meaning: the head form of its protocol

O-Send.payload.title: Payload level
O-Send.payload.meaning: $w \in V_{n}\llbracket\Theta_M \vdash U[x\cdot\bar\imath]\rrbracket$, \inmode{lf}{and $V_{n-\kappa_{give}}$ under a general table.}
O-Send.payload.why: The payload is read at the level of the continuation, because a send costs no level in the deadlock-free relation. \inmode{lf}{Under $\kappa_L$ it costs one.}
O-Send.payload.example: The payload $a$ of $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ at $Y\cdot 0$.

args.name: U[x\cdot\bar\imath]
args.meaning: the payload type with its point variables at the fields $x\cdot i$

O-Send.shift.title: $o : S@x^{+}$
O-Send.shift.meaning: The subject continues at $S$ and the next point $x^{+}$.
O-Send.shift.why: $x \prec x^{+}$ holds in every world, so successive actions on one end are ordered.

O-Recv.title: O-Recv
O-Recv.meaning: For every $j < n$ and every incoming $w \in V_j$ with ends disjoint from $\Theta$, the continuation is in $E_j$ with those ends added.
O-Recv.why: The value that arrives is unknown when the receiver is typed, so it continues for every value its type admits, and the compatibility of E-Recv pairs this with the sender's O-Send.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

args.name: S_0, S
args.meaning: the session type of the subject and its continuation after the head

O-Recv.forall.title: Every incoming value
O-Recv.forall.meaning: $\forall j, \Theta_{in}.\ j < n \land \Theta_{in} \mathbin{\#} \Theta \land w \in V_j\llbracket\Theta_{in} \vdash U[x\cdot\bar\imath]\rrbracket$.
O-Recv.forall.why: This negative occurrence of $V$ is at a lower level, so $V$ is well defined. \inmode{lf}{Under a general table the bound is $j + \kappa_{take} \leq n$, and $1 \leq \kappa_{take}$ keeps $j < n$.}
O-Recv.forall.signature: \forall j \in \mathbb{N}, \Theta_{in}.\ j + \kappa_{take} \leq n \land \Theta_{in} \mathbin{\#} \Theta \land w \in V_j\llbracket\Theta_{in} \vdash U[x\cdot\bar\imath]\rrbracket

args.name: j
args.meaning: the level of the incoming value

O-Recv.level.title: Continuation at level $j$
O-Recv.level.why: The continuation owns the old ends with $o$ advanced and the received ends, and is read at the level of the value it received.

args.name: j
args.meaning: the level of the incoming value

O-Close.title: O-Close
O-Close.why: After the close nobody holds $o$, which matches the restriction removed by the process rule.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Select.title: O-Select
O-Select.meaning: At a head $\oplus(S_1, S_2)$, $e'$ at $\Theta[o \mapsto S_i@\overline{x\cdot\kappa_i}]$.
O-Select.why: The selecting end keeps its name and moves to the dual side of the field of choice $i$, where E-Select places the end.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Branch.title: O-Branch
O-Branch.meaning: For the choice $i$ the step took, $e'$ at $\Theta[o \mapsto S_i@x\cdot\kappa_i]$, one level later.
O-Branch.why: The branching end moves to the field of choice $i$, the dual point of the selecting side.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Link.title: O-Link
O-Link.meaning: Two distinct ends at $x$ and $\overline{x}$ with dual types leave $\Theta$.
O-Link.why: After the link the partners of $o_1$ and $o_2$ form one channel, which is well typed only if $o_1$ and $o_2$ were dual.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

args.name: e, e'
args.meaning: a term and its successor, $e, e' \in \mathsf{Expr}$

O-Link.distinct.title: $o_1 \neq o_2$
O-Link.distinct.why: The link label is a set and may be degenerate.

O-Link.dual.title: Dual at dual points
O-Link.dual.why: E-Link types the two ends exactly dual at dual points, and the lock-free process relation keeps restricted pairs dual, which the renaming of the link preserves only under this condition.

args.name: S_1, S_2
args.meaning: the session types of the linked ends

rd.stable.title: $\mathsf{stable}\,t$
rd.stable.meaning: $\forall \alpha, t'.\ t \xrightarrow{\alpha} t' \Rightarrow \alpha \text{ is a session label}$.
rd.stable.why: Readiness constrains only terms that wait for a partner.

rd.offered.title: $\mathsf{offered}_\Theta(t, o)$
rd.offered.why: Each end has its own entry, so the offered ends are read off the labels.

rd.value.title: No offer means a value
rd.value.why: A stable term offering only ends it does not hold would be stuck.

rd.link.title: $\mathsf{link}\,t$
rd.link.meaning: $\exists os, t'.\ t \xrightarrow{\leftrightarrow os} t'$, and a term at a link is ready.
rd.link.why: A link step at process level needs no partner thread, so a link never waits and readiness need not order the link.
rd.link.breaks: Asking the order of a link would reject every link next to an end held at an unrelated point, and E-Link has no order premise.

args.name: os
args.meaning: the linked ends of the step

rd.below-rest.title: $\mathsf{below\_rest}$
rd.below-rest.meaning: Every offered end at $x$ lies below the dual point of every held end it does not offer and below every point of $F$.
rd.below-rest.why: It excludes circular waiting, because a waiting thread's offer is minimal among what it holds and what its context still does.
rd.below-rest.breaks: Client and server each blocked on their second channel while holding the first, under a cyclic order.
rd.below-rest.example: Closing $c$ at $\rho$ while $d$ is held at $\rho\cdot 0$ needs $\rho \prec \overline{\rho\cdot 0}$.

args.name: F
args.meaning: the future, a finite set of points

rd.below-held.title: Below held partners
rd.below-held.why: The partner of a held end acts at $\overline{x'}$, so the offered end is served before anyone waits on the held ends.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of an offered end

args.name: o', x'
args.meaning: a held end that is not offered and its point

rd.below-future.title: Below the future
rd.below-future.why: The context acts at the points of $F$ after the term returns.

args.name: x
args.meaning: the point of an offered end

rd.p-stable.title: $\mathsf{stable}\,p$
rd.p-stable.why: A process with an internal step is not waiting, and readiness speaks only of waiting processes.

rd.p-term.title: No offer means terminated
rd.p-term.why: A stable process that offers nothing to its environment must be finished, which is the deadlock-freedom statement at the process level.
rd.p-term.breaks: Without it, a stable process blocked on internal ends would satisfy P-Ready.

rd.above-offered.title: $\mathsf{above\_offered}$
rd.above-offered.meaning: Every interface end at $x$ that is not offered has an offered end at $x'$ with $W \vdash x' \prec \overline{x}$.
rd.above-offered.why: The environment can always serve some offered end first, so composing two ready processes over a strict world keeps one of them able to move.

args.name: o, x
args.meaning: an interface end that is not offered and its point

args.name: o', x'
args.meaning: an offered end and its point

P.strict.title: Strict later worlds only
P.strict.meaning: Each unfolding of $P$ holds in every $W_1 \sqsupseteq W$ with $\mathsf{strict}\,W_1$.
P.strict.why: In a cyclic $W_1$ a receive could bring ends that only a cyclic order accepts, and both components of a composition would be ready around the cycle.
P.strict.breaks: Two components each holding the partner of the other's second channel are both ready in a cyclic world and deadlock.

P.clauses.title: $\mathsf{clauses}_{W_1}(\Sigma', p')$
P.clauses.meaning: The stop, ready and step clauses of $p'$ at the interface $\Sigma'$ in the world $W_1$.
P.clauses.why: $P$ asks them after each fusion, and a term asks the same three of itself.
P.clauses.example: A finished process $(\varnothing, \{v\})$ meets them when $v \in V$.

P.fuse.title: Closed under fusions
P.fuse.meaning: Each unfolding holds at $(h, D)\cdot\Sigma$ and $(h, D)\cdot p$ for every $(h, D) \in \mathsf{Fus}(\Sigma, p)$.
P.fuse.why: Renaming, internalizing a pair of interface ends and the renaming done by a link are all fusions, and closure by definition makes each of them a projection.
P.fuse.breaks: With renamings alone, a link could join two unrelated interface ends into one channel and composition would fail.

P-Stop.title: P-Stop
P-Stop.meaning: $\mathsf{pirred}\,p' \Rightarrow \exists v, E.\ p' = (\varnothing, \{v\} \uplus E) \land v \in V\llbracket\Sigma' \vdash T\rrbracket \land \forall e \in E.\ e = \ast$.
P-Stop.why: An irreducible process in $P$ has no restricted channel left, its main thread returned a value in $V$ and every other thread returned $\ast$, which is the definition of terminated.
P-Stop.breaks: Without it, a process stuck with restricted channels would be in $P$, and adequacy would fail.

P-Ready.title: P-Ready
P-Ready.why: Readiness of processes excludes circular waiting across the interface.

P-Step.title: P-Step
P-Step.meaning: Every step $p' \xrightarrow{ev} p''$ meets $\mathsf{Pobl}_{ev}$. A process steps when some numbering of its threads steps, $p \xrightarrow{ev} p' \iff \exists q, q'.\ \mathsf{erase}\,q = p \land q \xrightarrow{ev} q' \land \mathsf{erase}\,q' = p'$.
P-Step.why: The obligations read the event and the result, and no thread number. Thread numbers matter only to the lock-free process relation, which records the thread holding each end.
P-Step.example: A message between two threads meets Q-Tau.

fuse.dcomm.title: $h$ commutes with duality
fuse.dcomm.why: Restricted channels and the partners added by Q-Send and Q-Recv enter $P$ as pairs, which $h$ must map to pairs.

fuse.inj.title: Injective on held ends
fuse.inj.meaning: $\forall o_1, o_2 \in \mathsf{held}.\ h(o_1) = h(o_2) \Rightarrow o_1 = o_2$.
fuse.inj.why: $\mathsf{csub}$ of a link identifies $\overline{o_1}$ and $o_2$, so $h$ is no bijection, but it is injective on the held ends of the other component.
fuse.inj.example: $\mathsf{csub}$ is injective on the other side's held ends.
fuse.inj.signature: \forall o_1, o_2 \in \mathsf{held}.\ h(o_1) = h(o_2) \Rightarrow o_1 = o_2

fuse.partners.title: New partners only on $D$
fuse.partners.why: Two held ends become partners only if they were or their channel is restricted by the fusion.
fuse.partners.breaks: Without it, $h$ joins unrelated interface ends into one channel, and composition fails.

fuse.D.title: $D \cap \mathsf{gch}_h[C] = \varnothing$
fuse.D.meaning: The channels restricted by the fusion are not images of channels already restricted.
fuse.D.why: Composition splits a fused process into its two sides, and this condition keeps the two restricted sets $\mathsf{gch}_h[C_i] \cup D_i$ disjoint from each other and from the interface.
fuse.D.breaks: Without it, a restricted channel could be restricted again as a new pair, and the split of the fused composite fails.

fuse.dpairs.title: $\mathsf{dpairs}\,D\,\Sigma$
fuse.dpairs.meaning: Both ends of every channel of $D$ are in $\Sigma$, at dual points and dual types.
fuse.dpairs.why: They become restricted, and restricted channels are dual pairs.

Q-Tau.title: Q-Tau
Q-Tau.meaning: An internal step that restricts no interface channel keeps $\Sigma$ and costs the levels of its kind of step.
Q-Tau.why: Administrative steps and internal synchronizations are one clause.
Q-Tau.example: A message between two threads costs one level\inmode{lf}{, and $\kappa_{give} + \kappa_{take}$ under a general table}.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

Q-Send.title: Q-Send
Q-Send.meaning: An external send. The interface part $\Sigma_v$ and the restricted part $\Theta_e$ of the payload leave, and the partners $\Sigma_e$ left behind join the interface.
Q-Send.why: It is O-Send at the process level, and the compatibility of P-Term discharges it from O-Send of the thread.
Q-Send.example: Sending a restricted end $d^{+}$ puts $d^{-}$ into the interface.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

args.name: \Sigma_v, \Sigma_r
args.meaning: the interface ends of the payload and the rest

args.name: \Theta_e, \Sigma_e
args.meaning: the restricted ends that leave and their partners that stay

Q-Send.theta-e.title: Extruded ends $\Theta_e$
Q-Send.theta-e.why: $\Theta_e$ is exactly the restricted part of the ends of $w$. Exactness of $V$ at the payload gives $\mathsf{fends}(w) = \mathrm{dom}\,\Sigma_v \cup \mathrm{dom}\,\Theta_e$, so the payload has $\mathsf{fends}(w)$ and nothing else.

args.name: \Theta_e
args.meaning: the restricted ends of the payload

args.name: \Sigma_v
args.meaning: the interface ends of the payload

Q-Send.split.title: $\mathsf{send\_split}$
Q-Send.split.meaning: The extruded ends are no interface ends, and $\Sigma_e$ holds the partners of extruded ends that stay, at dual types and points.
Q-Send.split.why: The partner of an extruded end becomes an interface end, and the interface must record its type and point.
Q-Send.split.breaks: Without it, the process would keep an end its interface does not mention, and P-Stop could not hold.

args.name: \Sigma_e
args.meaning: the partners that join the interface

Q-Send.sigma-e.title: $\Sigma_e$ joins the interface
Q-Send.sigma-e.meaning: Partners of extruded ends become interface ends.

Q-Recv.title: Q-Recv
Q-Recv.meaning: For every incoming environment and value, the process continues with the received ends added and the channels both of whose ends it now holds restricted.
Q-Recv.why: It is O-Recv at the process level, and composition feeds one component's Q-Send into the other's Q-Recv.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

Q-Recv.ok.title: $\mathsf{recv\_ok}$
Q-Recv.ok.meaning: Incoming ends are new to $\Sigma$, and every incoming end whose partner is held or received is at the dual point with the dual type.
Q-Recv.ok.why: Composition delivers one component's payload only under this condition, and it is what makes a newly restricted pair dual.
Q-Recv.ok.breaks: Without the duality conjunct, receiving the partner of a held end at a mismatched type would restrict an ill-typed channel.

Q-Recv.back.title: $\mathsf{recv\_back}$
Q-Recv.back.meaning: The channels of incoming ends whose partner is held or received along.
Q-Recv.back.why: Both ends of such a channel are now in the process, so it is restricted, as the interface stays partner-free.

Q-Recv.env.title: $\mathsf{recv\_env}$
Q-Recv.env.meaning: The interface after the receive, without the ends that became internal.
Q-Recv.env.why: Internal ends leave the interface, and the rest of $\Theta_2$ joins the interface.

Q-Link.title: Q-Close, Q-Select, Q-Branch, Q-Link
Q-Link.meaning: The term obligations O-Close, O-Select, O-Branch and O-Link with $\Sigma$ for $\Theta$ and $P$ for $E$.
Q-Link.why: An external close, choice or link acts on interface ends exactly as a thread acts on its own ends.
Q-Link.example: Q-Link removes both linked ends from $\Sigma$.

args.name: p, p'
args.meaning: the process before and after the step, $p = (C, E)$ and $p' = (C', E')$

sj.at.title: Judgment at a set of points $X$
sj.at.meaning: For every level, later world, environment $\Theta'$ disjoint from the ends $|\Delta|$ and grounding $\gamma$ of the variables of $\Delta$ in $\Theta'$, $\gamma(e) \in E_n\llbracket|\Delta| \cup \Theta' \vdash T\rrbracket^{X}$.
sj.at.why: It quantifies over everything a context may supply, so it composes by the compatibility lemmas.

args.name: \Delta
args.meaning: the linear context of the typing judgment, its ends erased to $|\Delta|$

args.name: X
args.meaning: a set of points read as the future

args.name: n, W', \Theta', \gamma
args.meaning: every level, extension, environment of the grounding and grounding

sj.grel.title: Grounding $\gamma \in G\llbracket\Theta \vdash \Delta\rrbracket$
sj.grel.meaning: $\gamma$ substitutes for each entry $T^a$ of $\Delta$ a value in $V\llbracket\Theta_i \vdash T\rrbracket$, with $\Theta = \biguplus_i \Theta_i$.
sj.grel.why: Variables of $\Delta$ stand for values, and the ends of those values split $\Theta$ disjointly.

args.name: \gamma
args.meaning: a substitution $\mathbb{N} \to \mathsf{Expr}$ for the variables of $\Delta$

sj.den.title: $\mathsf{den}_{\rho,B}(F)$
sj.den.meaning: $\mathsf{den}_{\rho,B}(F_1, f) = F_1 \cup \rho(\varphi) \cup B$, with $\rho(\varphi)$ only if $f$ has the variable $\varphi$ and $B$ only if $f$ has the flag $\bot$.
sj.den.why: A future variable and the flag $\bot$ stand for unknown sets of points, so the judgment holds at each choice of these sets.

sj.term.title: $\Delta \vDash^{F}_W e : T$
sj.term.meaning: $\forall \rho, B.\ \Delta \vDash^{\mathsf{den}_{\rho,B}(F)}_W e : T$, with the same context $\Delta$ as the typing judgment.
sj.term.why: It is the conclusion of the fundamental theorem for terms. \inmode{lf}{The lock-free reading $\vDash[\kappa_L]$ uses the table $\kappa_L$.}

sj.proc.title: $\Sigma \vDash_W p : T$
sj.proc.why: Adequacy turns it into deadlock freedom. \inmode{lf}{With $\kappa_L$ it also gives absence of internal divergence.}

fu.zero.title: Level $0$
fu.zero.why: Step indexing starts from the trivial predicate.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: the result, a credited type or $\mathsf{thread}$

args.name: d
args.meaning: the frame, the actions left before returning, $d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

args.name: r
args.meaning: the reserve, the tickets kept on return, $r \in \mathbb{N}$

fu.rty.title: Result $\sigma$
fu.rty.meaning: $\sigma$ is a credited type $T^a$ of the returned value, or $\mathsf{thread}$, whose value holds no end.
fu.rty.why: A spawned thread returns $\ast$ and keeps no end, which $\mathsf{thread}$ states without a type.
fu.rty.example: $\mathsf{thread}$ for a lock-free process relation thread.

fu.frame.title: Frame $d$
fu.frame.meaning: $d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ bounds the channel actions the term performs before it returns.
fu.frame.why: Every action asks $1 \leq d$ and lowers $d$ by one, so the frame bounds how often the context decrements its own ends during the term.

fu.reserve.title: Reserve $r$
fu.reserve.meaning: $r \in \mathbb{N}$ is the number of tickets the term must still hold when it returns.
fu.reserve.why: The context of the term uses these tickets on its own links afterwards, which the ticket need of the term guarantees through $\vartheta(r) \leq tk$.
fu.reserve.breaks: Without a reserve, a term could use tickets its context needs, and a context link would find $tk = 0$.

fu.Phi.title: Held ends $\Phi$
fu.Phi.meaning: $\Phi$ maps each end the thread holds to its protocol $S$, a session type with annotations, and its counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, written $o \mapsto S^{f}$. In the Rocq these are two maps $\Pi$ and $\varphi$ with one domain.
fu.Phi.why: The counter bounds how many actions of the thread holding it may pass before the end acts again, and the protocol says when the end is idle and what it sends and receives. Where the relation gives an end a point, fuel gives it a counter.

args.name: S^{f}
args.meaning: the protocol $S$ and counter $f$ of an end

fu.tick.title: $\Phi{\downarrow}$
fu.tick.meaning: Every counter of $\Phi$ lowered by one, truncated at $0$, with $\infty$ kept.
fu.tick.why: An action decrements the counters of the other ends of the thread holding it, and a transfer passes counters on one lower. Both use this operation.
fu.tick.example: $\{a \mapsto S^{3}, b \mapsto S'^{1}\}{\downarrow} = \{a \mapsto S^{2}, b \mapsto S'\inmode{lf}{^{0}}\}$.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

fu.tk.title: Tickets $tk$
fu.tk.meaning: $tk \in \mathbb{N}$ is the thread's count of link tickets.
fu.tk.why: Each link uses one ticket and tickets are conserved, so a thread performs finitely many links between actions.

fu.refill-kripke.title: Every counter bound above $N$
fu.refill-kripke.meaning: Fuel at $N$ holds at every $N'$ with $N \sqsubseteq_{\mathsf{rle}} N'$, where finite counter bounds are ordered by $\leq$ and $\infty$ lies above $\infty$ only.
fu.refill-kripke.why: A received value may be used at a larger counter bound, and $\infty$ must stay separate because a box received at $\infty$ guarantees nothing at finite instances.
fu.refill-kripke.breaks: With $\leq$ on $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, a thread at $N = 2$ could receive a box typed at $\infty$ and fail at its finite instance.

fu.rename.title: Injective renamings
fu.rename.meaning: Fuel holds for every renaming $g$ of ends injective on $\mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$.
fu.rename.why: A link renames the partner of a removed end in another thread, so fuel must remain renaming.
fu.rename.breaks: A renaming that merges two held ends would merge their counters.

fu.val.title: (val)
fu.val.why: A returning term transfers its context the reserve it promised and a value whose counters meet its credits, which the bind lemma of fuel consumes.
fu.val.breaks: Without $r \leq tk$, a context link after the term could find no ticket.
fu.val.signature: g(e) \in \mathsf{Val} \Rightarrow r \leq tk \land g(e) \in FV^{N'}_{n+1}\llbracket g\Phi \vdash \sigma \rrbracket

args.name: g, N'
args.meaning: the renaming and the counter bound

fu.step.title: (step)
fu.step.why: Each step updates the state by one index-free rule, which the lock-free process relation follows along a run.

args.name: \alpha, e'
args.meaning: the step label and the successor

fu.oneclock.title: One level per step
fu.oneclock.meaning: Every step costs one level, $\beta$, creation, spawn and link included.
fu.oneclock.why: A clock that let $\beta$ be free would admit a box that only takes $\beta$ steps at every level, so the cost fundamental theorem would need the guard as a premise.

F-Wait.title: F-Wait
F-Wait.meaning: $\Phi(o) = S^{f}$ with $S$ not idle, so the end is held and can act.
F-Wait.why: An idle end is exempt from the checks $\geq 1$, so it must not act either.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

F-Tick.title: F-Count
F-Tick.meaning: $\mathsf{positive}(\Phi \setminus o)$, every other end that is not idle has counter at least $1$.
F-Tick.why: Each action decrements the counters of the other ends, so an end can wait only as many actions of the thread holding it as its counter allows.
F-Tick.breaks: A holding thread that loops on other ends forever while its partner waits on a held end.
F-Tick.example: At $\Phi = \{a \mapsto S^{2}, b \mapsto S'\inmode{lf}{^{0}}\}$ no action on $a$ is allowed unless $b$ is idle.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

F-Tick.frame.title: $1 \leq d$
F-Tick.frame.meaning: The frame has a unit for the action.
F-Tick.frame.why: The frame bounds the decrements of the context's ends during the term.

fu.idle.title: $\mathsf{idle}$
fu.idle.why: Idleness removes the checks $\geq 1$ and never changes how a counter evolves, so counters stay index-free. The typing ages idle ends by truncation at $0$, matching counters that decrement down to $0$.
fu.idle.breaks: An idle end whose credit stayed fixed while its counter decrements would exceed its counter.

F-Beta.title: F-Beta
F-Beta.why: A $\beta$ step changes no counter and costs one level.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

args.name: \sigma
args.meaning: the result, a credited type or $\mathsf{thread}$

args.name: d
args.meaning: the frame, the actions left before returning, $d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

args.name: r
args.meaning: the reserve, the tickets kept on return, $r \in \mathbb{N}$

F-New.title: F-New
F-New.meaning: For a fresh $c$, some $S$ adds $c^{+} \mapsto S\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$ and $c^{-} \mapsto \overline{S}\inmode{lf}{^{N}}$ to $\Phi$.
F-New.why: A new channel starts with both ends at the counter bound $N$, the credit E-New gives to fresh ends.

F-New.fresh.title: Fresh against the thread
F-New.fresh.why: Without it, a new channel could reuse a held name and overwrite its counter.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

F-New.cnew.title: New ends at $N$
F-New.cnew.why: One counter bound $N$ serves fresh ends and ends after an action.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

F-Spawn.title: F-Spawn
F-Spawn.meaning: The child takes $\Phi|_M{\downarrow}$ for $M = \mathsf{fends}(v)$ and $\lceil tk/2 \rceil$ tickets and runs as a thread, the parent keeps $\Phi \setminus M$ and $\lfloor tk/2 \rfloor$.
F-Spawn.why: The split is a function of $v$ and $tk$, so it is the same at each level.
F-Spawn.example: The thunk takes $d'$ at $1$ in the cycle.

F-Spawn.held.title: $M \subseteq \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$
F-Spawn.held.why: A child mentioning an end the parent does not hold would act on an end without a counter.
F-Spawn.held.breaks: A box mentioning channel constants would pass on ends nobody holds.

fu.fspare.title: $\mathsf{positive}$
fu.fspare.meaning: $\mathsf{positive}(\Phi) \iff$ every end of $\Phi$ that is not idle has counter at least $1$.
fu.fspare.why: A transfer passes the counter minus one, so a non-idle end must have a positive counter. A spawn is no action, so this is its only check.
fu.fspare.breaks: A transfer at counter $0$ under truncation passes $0$ again and an end is passed on forever.

args.name: \Phi
args.meaning: the held ends, a finite map $o \mapsto S^{f}$ from ends to a protocol and a counter $f \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$

F-Spawn.child.title: The child
F-Spawn.child.why: The child is a new lock-free process relation thread, so it must have thread fuel at exactly the ends, counters and tickets the lock-free process relation moves to the child.

F-Spawn.tickets.title: Ticket split
F-Spawn.tickets.why: A fixed split is the only split independent of the level.

F-Send.title: F-Send
F-Send.meaning: An action on $o$ that passes on $M = \mathsf{fends}(w)$ one lower, the payload in $FV$, and the continuation with $o$ back at $N$.
F-Send.why: A send is an action, so F-Count applies, and a transfer, so $\mathsf{positive}$ applies.
F-Send.example: $\mathsf{send}\,\langle a, y\rangle$ in the growing ring.

F-Send.notsubj.title: $o \notin M \subseteq \mathrm{dom}\,\Phi$
F-Send.notsubj.meaning: A send gives away held ends other than its subject.
F-Send.notsubj.why: The continuation keeps acting on $o$, so $o$ cannot leave.
F-Send.notsubj.breaks: A term that sends its own subject or an end its context holds.

F-Send.payload.title: Payload in $FV$
F-Send.payload.meaning: $w \in FV^N_n\llbracket\Phi|_M{\downarrow} \vdash T\rrbracket$, with every transferred counter lowered by one transfer.
